ingredients.name: aspartame
ingredients.explanation: An artificial sweetener. Classified as possibly cancer causing.
ingredients.notes: IARC Group 2B since July 2023. JECFA maintained safe ADI of 40mg/kg. CSPI rates Avoid.

ingredients.name: acesulfame potassium
ingredients.explanation: An artificial sweetener. Poorly tested. Some studies raise cancer concerns.
ingredients.notes: CSPI rates Avoid due to inadequate testing. FDA and EFSA consider safe within limits.

ingredients.name: saccharin
ingredients.explanation: An artificial sweetener. Once linked to bladder cancer in rats but later cleared.
ingredients.notes: IARC removed from Group 2B in 1999 after reviewing human data. Current consensus is safe. CSPI now rates Caution only. IARC Group 3 (not classifiable). Was delisted from NTP RoC in 2000. CSPI rates Avoid.

ingredients.name: sucralose
ingredients.explanation: An artificial sweetener. Some studies suggest it may affect gut bacteria.
ingredients.notes: CSPI rates Caution. Recent studies on DNA damage and gut microbiome effects.

ingredients.name: stevia
ingredients.explanation: A plant-based sweetener. No known health risks.
ingredients.notes: CSPI rates Safe. FDA GRAS. Derived from stevia plant leaves.

ingredients.name: neotame
ingredients.explanation: An artificial sweetener. Approved as safe by major regulators.
ingredients.notes: FDA approved. EFSA approved. Limited independent research.

ingredients.name: erythritol
ingredients.explanation: A sugar alcohol. Recent studies link it to blood clotting risks.
ingredients.notes: 2023 Cleveland Clinic study linked to cardiovascular events. More research needed.

ingredients.name: xylitol
ingredients.explanation: A sugar alcohol. Safe for humans. Can have a laxative effect in large amounts.
ingredients.notes: Toxic to dogs. CSPI rates Certain People Should Avoid due to GI effects.

ingredients.name: sorbitol
ingredients.explanation: A sugar alcohol. Safe in normal amounts. May cause bloating in excess.
ingredients.notes: GRAS status. Common in sugar-free products.

ingredients.name: red 3
ingredients.explanation: An artificial color. Linked to thyroid tumors in studies.
ingredients.notes: FDA banned Jan 2025 (enforcement 2027). EU banned. Causes thyroid tumors in rats. CSPI rates Avoid.

ingredients.name: red 40
ingredients.explanation: An artificial color. Linked to hyperactivity in children. Being phased out.
ingredients.notes: FDA voluntary phase-out by end 2026. EU requires warning label. CSPI rates Caution. Linked to behavioral issues in children.

ingredients.name: yellow 5
ingredients.explanation: An artificial color. Linked to hyperactivity in children. May trigger allergies.
ingredients.notes: FDA voluntary phase-out by end 2026. EU requires warning label. CSPI rates Caution.

ingredients.name: yellow 6
ingredients.explanation: An artificial color. Linked to hyperactivity in children. Contains carcinogenic contaminants.
ingredients.notes: FDA voluntary phase-out by end 2026. EU warning label required. CSPI rates Caution.

ingredients.name: blue 1
ingredients.explanation: An artificial color. Limited safety data. Being phased out as a precaution.
ingredients.notes: FDA voluntary phase-out by end 2026. CSPI rates Caution. Some studies show it may cross blood-brain barrier.

ingredients.name: blue 2
ingredients.explanation: An artificial color. Poorly tested. Being phased out as a precaution.
ingredients.notes: FDA voluntary phase-out by end 2026. CSPI rates Caution.

ingredients.name: green 3
ingredients.explanation: An artificial color. Limited testing. Being phased out as a precaution.
ingredients.notes: FDA voluntary phase-out by end 2026. Banned in EU. CSPI rates Caution.

ingredients.name: caramel color
ingredients.explanation: A common coloring. Some types contain 4-MEI, a possibly cancer causing byproduct.
ingredients.notes: IARC Group 2B applies to 4-MEI byproduct only at high doses, not caramel color itself. Moderate risk maintained. Class III and IV caramel colors contain 4-MEI (IARC Group 2B). CSPI rates Caution for Class III/IV. Class I and II are safe.

ingredients.name: titanium dioxide
ingredients.explanation: A whitening agent. Possibly cancer causing. May damage DNA.
ingredients.notes: IARC Group 2B. EU banned in 2022 after EFSA found genotoxicity concerns. FDA still allows.

ingredients.name: annatto
ingredients.explanation: A natural color from seeds. No known health risks.
ingredients.notes: Natural plant-based colorant. GRAS.

ingredients.name: beta-carotene
ingredients.explanation: A natural orange pigment. Converts to Vitamin A in the body.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Found naturally in carrots and sweet potatoes.

ingredients.name: carmine
ingredients.explanation: A natural red color made from insects. Safe but may cause allergies in rare cases.
ingredients.notes: Derived from cochineal insects. CSPI rates Certain People Should Avoid due to rare allergic reactions.

ingredients.name: sodium nitrite
ingredients.explanation: Found in processed meats. Forms cancer causing compounds when heated.
ingredients.notes: IARC Group 1 carcinogen (as used in processed meats). Rule 4 applied: IARC classification overrides other ratings.

ingredients.name: sodium nitrate
ingredients.explanation: Found in cured meats. Converts to nitrite in the body. Linked to cancer risk.
ingredients.notes: Converts to sodium nitrite. Same cancer concerns. CSPI rates Caution.

ingredients.name: sodium benzoate
ingredients.explanation: A common preservative. Can form benzene (a carcinogen) when mixed with vitamin C.
ingredients.notes: CSPI rates Caution. Benzene formation with ascorbic acid is the main concern.

ingredients.name: potassium sorbate
ingredients.explanation: A common preservative. No known health risks at normal levels.
ingredients.notes: CSPI rates Safe. GRAS. Widely used in cheese, wine, baked goods.

ingredients.name: bha
ingredients.explanation: A preservative. Linked to cancer in animal studies. Under safety review.
ingredients.notes: IARC Group 2B. NTP: reasonably anticipated carcinogen. FDA launched safety review Feb 2026. EU banned. West Virginia banned. CSPI rates Avoid.

ingredients.name: bht
ingredients.explanation: A preservative. May disrupt hormones. Under safety review.
ingredients.notes: EU banned due to endocrine disruption concerns. FDA launched safety review Aug 2025. CSPI rates Caution.

ingredients.name: potassium bromate
ingredients.explanation: A flour improver. Linked to kidney damage and tumors.
ingredients.notes: IARC Group 2B. Banned in EU since 1990, India since 2016. US still allows. CSPI rates Avoid.

ingredients.name: tbhq
ingredients.explanation: A preservative in oils and snacks. May affect immune system at high doses.
ingredients.notes: CSPI rates Caution. Limited evidence of harm but poorly studied long-term.

ingredients.name: propylparaben
ingredients.explanation: A preservative. May disrupt hormones. Linked to reproductive issues.
ingredients.notes: EU banned in food since 2006. Endocrine disruptor. California banning from 2027. CSPI rates Avoid.

ingredients.name: sulfites
ingredients.explanation: Preservatives in wine, dried fruit. Safe for most. Can trigger asthma in sensitive people.
ingredients.notes: CSPI rates Certain People Should Avoid. FDA requires label declaration. Can cause severe reactions in asthmatics.

ingredients.name: calcium propionate
ingredients.explanation: A bread preservative. Prevents mold. No known health risks.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Widely used in bakery products.

ingredients.name: monosodium glutamate
ingredients.explanation: A flavor enhancer. Safe for most people. Some may experience mild sensitivity.
ingredients.notes: FDA GRAS. WHO/JECFA safe. EFSA set ADI of 30mg/kg. CSPI rates Certain People Should Avoid.

ingredients.name: disodium inosinate
ingredients.explanation: A flavor enhancer often paired with MSG. No known health risks.
ingredients.notes: Usually used with MSG. GRAS.

ingredients.name: disodium guanylate
ingredients.explanation: A flavor enhancer often paired with MSG. No known health risks.
ingredients.notes: Usually used with MSG. GRAS.

ingredients.name: hydrolyzed vegetable protein
ingredients.explanation: A flavor enhancer. Contains naturally occurring glutamate. Safe for most.
ingredients.notes: Contains free glutamic acid similar to MSG.

ingredients.name: autolyzed yeast extract
ingredients.explanation: A natural flavor enhancer. Contains glutamate. Safe for most people.
ingredients.notes: Natural source of umami flavor.

ingredients.name: carrageenan
ingredients.explanation: From seaweed. Some studies link it to gut inflammation.
ingredients.notes: IARC Group 2B applies only to degraded carrageenan (poligeenan), not food-grade undegraded carrageenan. Kept moderate. Degraded carrageenan (poligeenan) is IARC Group 2B. Food-grade carrageenan is debated. CSPI rates Caution.

ingredients.name: soy lecithin
ingredients.explanation: A common emulsifier from soybeans. Safe. May be from GMO sources.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Very widely used. Allergen for soy-sensitive individuals.

ingredients.name: xanthan gum
ingredients.explanation: A natural thickener. No known health risks.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Produced by bacterial fermentation.

ingredients.name: guar gum
ingredients.explanation: A natural thickener from guar beans. No known health risks.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. India is the world's largest producer.

ingredients.name: polysorbate 80
ingredients.explanation: An emulsifier. Some studies suggest it may harm gut lining.
ingredients.notes: Animal studies show gut inflammation. More human research needed.

ingredients.name: mono and diglycerides
aliases: mono- and diglycerides of fatty acids
ingredients.explanation: Common emulsifiers. Made from fats. No known health risks.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Very widely used in baked goods and margarine.

ingredients.name: pectin
ingredients.explanation: A natural gelling agent from fruits. No known health risks.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Found naturally in apples and citrus fruits.

ingredients.name: azodicarbonamide
ingredients.explanation: A dough conditioner. Also used in yoga mats. Breaks down into carcinogens when baked.
ingredients.notes: Banned in EU, UK, Australia. Decomposes into semicarbazide and urethane (carcinogens). CSPI rates Avoid.

ingredients.name: brominated vegetable oil
ingredients.explanation: Used in citrus drinks. Linked to nerve and thyroid damage.
ingredients.notes: FDA banned Aug 2024. Was banned in EU and Japan decades ago. FSSAI also banned.

ingredients.name: high fructose corn syrup
ingredients.explanation: A cheap sweetener. Excess consumption linked to obesity and fatty liver disease.
ingredients.notes: CSPI rates Cut Back. Not toxic per se but over-consumed. WHO recommends limiting free sugars.

ingredients.name: maltodextrin
ingredients.explanation: A processed starch. Can spike blood sugar quickly. May affect gut bacteria.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. High glycemic index. Studies suggest impact on gut microbiome.

ingredients.name: partially hydrogenated oil
ingredients.explanation: The main source of artificial trans fats. Directly linked to heart disease.
ingredients.notes: FDA revoked GRAS status in 2018. WHO called for global elimination. Banned in EU and India.

ingredients.name: natural flavoring
ingredients.explanation: A vague term. Could be many different substances. Safety cannot be confirmed.
ingredients.notes: Umbrella term. Can include hundreds of unlisted chemicals. No way to verify specific contents.

ingredients.name: artificial flavor
ingredients.explanation: Lab-made flavoring chemicals. Exact ingredients are usually not disclosed.
ingredients.notes: Umbrella term. Individual chemicals may vary in safety. Lack of transparency is the concern.

ingredients.name: phosphoric acid
ingredients.explanation: Found in cola drinks. Excess intake linked to weakened bones.
ingredients.notes: CSPI rates Cut Back. Not toxic but over-consumption affects calcium absorption.

ingredients.name: acrylamide
ingredients.explanation: Forms in starchy foods cooked at high heat. A known cancer risk.
ingredients.notes: IARC Group 2A. Not an additive but forms during cooking (frying, baking). Found in chips, fries, bread.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.explanation: Just water. Nothing to worry about.

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.explanation: Common table salt. Safe in normal amounts.
ingredients.notes: CSPI rates Cut Back due to over-consumption. Safe as an ingredient.

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.explanation: Common sugar. Safe as an ingredient. Best consumed in moderation.
ingredients.notes: CSPI rates Cut Back. WHO recommends limiting free sugars to <10% of energy intake.

ingredients.name: milk
ingredients.explanation: A common dairy ingredient. Safe. Allergen for those with lactose intolerance.
ingredients.notes: Major allergen. Must be declared on food labels.

ingredients.name: butter

ingredients.name: olive oil

ingredients.name: sunflower oil

ingredients.name: palm oil
ingredients.explanation: High in saturated fat. Raises LDL cholesterol. Refined version contains processing contaminants.
ingredients.notes: IARC classifications are for processing contaminants GE(2A) and 3-MCPD(2B) formed during refining, not palm oil itself. AHA advises limiting intake due to high saturated fat (50%) raising LDL cholesterol. WHO developing tropical oils guidelines (2024). Refined palm oil contains glycidyl esters (IARC Group 2A) and 3-MCPD (IARC Group 2B) as processing contaminants. EFSA enforces strict GE limits especially in infant food. Cold-pressed unrefined red palm oil is safer and rich in carotenoids and vitamin E tocotrienols. 2025 US Dietary Guidelines: replacing palm oil with unsaturated vegetable oils decreases LDL-C. Environmental concern: major driver of tropical deforestation.

ingredients.notes: Allergen for soy-sensitive individuals.

ingredients.name: baking soda

ingredients.explanation: A common baking ingredient. Completely safe.

ingredients.notes: CSPI rates Cut Back. Different from high fructose corn syrup.

ingredients.notes: GRAS. CSPI rates Safe.

ingredients.notes: GRAS.

ingredients.name: sodium alginate

ingredients.notes: GRAS.

ingredients.name: sorbic acid

ingredients.notes: GRAS status in US. CSPI rates Safe. JECFA ADI established.

ingredients.name: benzoic acid

ingredients.name: potassium nitrate

ingredients.notes: IARC Group 2A when ingested. Rule 4 applied: IARC classification overrides other ratings. CSPI rates Avoid.

ingredients.name: calcium sorbate
ingredients.explanation: Calcium salt of sorbic acid. Same safety profile as sorbic acid. Well-studied.

ingredients.name: potassium benzoate
ingredients.explanation: Potassium salt of benzoic acid. Same benzene-forming risk when mixed with vitamin C.
ingredients.notes: CSPI rates Caution. Functionally same as sodium benzoate. Common in soft drinks.

ingredients.name: propionic acid
ingredients.explanation: Naturally occurs in swiss cheese. Widely used mold inhibitor in bread products.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. CSPI rates Safe. Naturally produced in fermented foods.

ingredients.name: glucono delta lactone
ingredients.explanation: Natural acid found in fruit and honey. Used in silken tofu production. Very safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Used in cheese, meat, and tofu production. CSPI rates Safe.

ingredients.name: fumaric acid
ingredients.explanation: Naturally found in plants and mushrooms. Used as a sour flavoring agent.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Produced naturally in the body during metabolism. Very low intake levels.

ingredients.name: succinic acid
ingredients.explanation: Naturally present in meat, vegetables, and wine. Used as a flavoring agent.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Produced naturally in the body. Very minimal dietary exposure.

ingredients.name: adipic acid
ingredients.explanation: Mild organic acid used in powdered drink mixes. Naturally found in beet juice.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Low use levels. Mainly used in gelatin-based desserts and powdered drinks.

ingredients.name: calcium chloride
ingredients.explanation: Salt used to keep canned vegetables firm and make tofu. Also adds calcium.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Widely used in cheese-making and canning. Also used in sports drinks for electrolytes.

ingredients.name: potassium phosphate
ingredients.explanation: Phosphate salt used as a buffer in food. Widely used and generally safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. High phosphate intake from multiple sources should be monitored by kidney patients.

ingredients.name: ammonium carbonate
ingredients.explanation: Old-fashioned leavening agent used before modern baking powder. Leaves no residue.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Fully decomposes during baking. Used in Scandinavian cookies and crackers.

ingredients.name: calcium disodium edta
ingredients.explanation: Chelating agent in canned foods. May interfere with zinc and mineral absorption.
ingredients.notes: CSPI rates Caution. Long-term intake may affect mineral absorption. Strict limits apply.

ingredients.name: propyl gallate
ingredients.explanation: Synthetic antioxidant used in oils. Animal studies showed tumor activity at high doses.
ingredients.notes: CSPI rates Caution. NTP studies found some tumor activity in animals. Human data limited.

ingredients.name: natamycin
ingredients.explanation: Natural antifungal from bacteria. Used on cheese rinds. Not absorbed into the food.
ingredients.notes: JECFA ADI established. Only used on food surface. Not absorbed into the food itself.

ingredients.name: lysozyme

ingredients.name: nisin
ingredients.explanation: Natural antimicrobial peptide from bacteria. Used in processed cheese. Very safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. One of the oldest natural food preservatives. Very low effective dose needed.

ingredients.name: dimethyl dicarbonate

ingredients.name: hexamethylene tetramine
ingredients.explanation: Releases formaldehyde in acidic foods. Banned in the US. Formaldehyde concerns.
ingredients.notes: Banned in US as food additive. EU allows limited use in provolone cheese only.

ingredients.name: ethylene oxide
ingredients.explanation: Fumigant used on spices and dried herbs. Classified as a known carcinogen.
ingredients.notes: IARC Group 1 carcinogen. Banned for food use in EU. US allows limited spice treatment only.

ingredients.name: formic acid
ingredients.explanation: Found in ants and stinging nettles. Used as a preservative in some countries.
ingredients.notes: Not approved for direct food use in the US. Limited ADI set by JECFA.

ingredients.name: stearic acid
ingredients.explanation: Natural saturated fat found in meat and cocoa. Does not raise bad cholesterol.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Unlike most saturated fats, stearic acid is considered neutral for heart health.

ingredients.name: quinoline yellow
ingredients.explanation: Synthetic dye. Banned in US and Australia. Hyperactivity concerns in children.
ingredients.notes: CSPI rates Avoid. Not approved for food use in the US or Australia. EU requires warning label.

ingredients.name: carmoisine
ingredients.explanation: Red synthetic azo dye. Banned in US, Canada, Japan. Hyperactivity concerns.
ingredients.notes: CSPI rates Avoid. Banned in multiple countries. EU requires hyperactivity warning on label.

ingredients.name: amaranth dye
ingredients.explanation: Red synthetic dye. Banned in the US since 1976 due to cancer concerns in animals.
ingredients.notes: CSPI rates Avoid. US banned it in 1976. EU permits limited use only. Not the same as amaranth grain.

ingredients.name: ponceau 4r
ingredients.explanation: Red synthetic azo dye. Banned in the US and Canada. Hyperactivity link in children.
ingredients.notes: CSPI rates Avoid. Not approved in the US. EU requires hyperactivity warning. Used in India.

ingredients.name: chlorophylls
ingredients.explanation: Green pigment from plants. Natural and safe. Commonly used in foods and drinks.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Derived from nettles, grass, and spinach. No known health concerns.

ingredients.name: copper chlorophyllin
ingredients.explanation: Stabilized green color made from chlorophyll. Safe at normal food use levels.
ingredients.notes: Stable version of chlorophyll. Used in green-colored candies and drinks. JECFA reviewed.

ingredients.name: plain caramel
ingredients.explanation: Caramel made only from heat and sugar. No additives. Safest caramel class.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Simplest form of caramel coloring. Used in spirits and beer.

ingredients.name: caustic sulfite caramel
ingredients.explanation: Caramel color made with sulfite compounds. Used in some spirits. Low risk.
ingredients.notes: JECFA ADI set. Less common than Class III and IV. Used in cognac and spirits.

ingredients.name: ammonia caramel
ingredients.explanation: Caramel made using ammonia. Contains 4-methylimidazole, a possible carcinogen.
ingredients.notes: IARC Group 2B for 4-MEI at high doses in animal studies. Caramel itself not classified. Moderate maintained. 4-MEI byproduct is IARC Group 2B. California requires cancer warning above certain levels.

ingredients.name: sulfite ammonia caramel
ingredients.explanation: Most common caramel used in colas. Contains 4-MEI, a possible carcinogen.
ingredients.notes: IARC Group 2B for 4-MEI byproduct at high animal doses. Human risk at food levels is debated. Moderate maintained. CSPI rates Caution. 4-MEI is IARC Group 2B. Used in Coca-Cola and similar dark soft drinks.

ingredients.name: lycopene
ingredients.explanation: Natural red pigment from tomatoes. Also an antioxidant. Very safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Studied for potential health benefits. Found naturally in tomatoes and pink grapefruit.

ingredients.name: beetroot red
ingredients.explanation: Red color from beets. Natural. May turn urine pink in some people. Completely harmless.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. The urine-pinking effect (beeturia) is harmless. Widely used in natural food products.

ingredients.name: anthocyanins
ingredients.explanation: Natural blue-red pigments from berries, grapes, and red cabbage. Safe and antioxidant-rich.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Color varies with pH. Found naturally in many fruits and vegetables.

ingredients.name: magnesium carbonate
ingredients.explanation: Natural mineral used as an anti-caking agent and acidity regulator. Very safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Also used as a magnesium supplement. Common in table salt and icing sugar.

ingredients.name: konjac glucomannan
ingredients.explanation: Natural dietary fiber from konjac plant. Excellent thickener. May help blood sugar.
ingredients.notes: Very high water absorption. Choking risk flagged for mini-jelly cups. Otherwise safe.

ingredients.name: tara gum
ingredients.explanation: Natural seed gum from the tara plant in Peru. Safe thickener and stabilizer.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Similar properties to guar gum. Relatively new but well-reviewed additive.

ingredients.name: cassia gum
ingredients.explanation: Seed gum from cassia plants. Used in pet food and cheese. Safe for humans.
ingredients.notes: EFSA approved with limits. Commonly used in cheese and meat products.

ingredients.name: hydroxypropyl cellulose
ingredients.explanation: Modified plant fiber used as a thickener and coating agent. Not absorbed by the body.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Passes through the body undigested. Used in tablet coatings and sauces.

ingredients.name: methyl cellulose
ingredients.explanation: Cellulose modified to thicken and gel. Used in plant-based meat products. Not digested.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Key ingredient in plant-based burgers. Gels when heated, unlike most gels.

ingredients.name: sodium carbonate
ingredients.explanation: Mineral salt used to regulate acidity in noodles and baked goods. Very safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Used in Asian noodles and as a water softener. Natural mineral compound.

ingredients.name: magnesium hydroxide
ingredients.explanation: Natural mineral used to regulate acidity. Also sold as an antacid. Very safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Long history of use as a safe antacid. Used in cocoa processing and baked goods.

ingredients.name: calcium hydroxide
ingredients.explanation: Used to firm pickled vegetables and process corn (nixtamalization). Traditional and safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Used in traditional Indian paan as chuna. Central to making masa for tortillas.

ingredients.name: potassium hydroxide
ingredients.explanation: Strong alkali used to cure olives and pretzels. Safe at trace food use levels.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Fully neutralized in final food product. No residual alkalinity in finished food.

ingredients.name: disodium ribonucleotides
ingredients.explanation: Blend of disodium inosinate and disodium guanylate. Boosts umami flavor powerfully.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Not suitable for gout sufferers due to purine content. Often used with MSG.

ingredients.name: beeswax
ingredients.explanation: Natural wax from bees used to coat fruits and candies. Safe for most people.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Not vegan. Used on apples, citrus, and confectionery as a surface coating.

ingredients.name: carnauba wax
ingredients.explanation: Plant-based wax from Brazilian palm leaves. Used as a glaze on candy and fruits.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Vegan. Very common on jelly beans and pharmaceutical tablets. No safety concerns.

ingredients.name: shellac
ingredients.explanation: Resin secreted by lac bugs. Used to glaze candy and fruits. Not vegan.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Not suitable for vegans or strict vegetarians. Common on candy-coated chocolates.

ingredients.name: nitrogen gas
ingredients.explanation: Inert gas used in food packaging to prevent oxidation. Completely safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Makes up 78% of air. Extends shelf life of chips and snacks safely.

ingredients.name: carbon dioxide
ingredients.explanation: Gas used for carbonation and food preservation. Natural and safe at food levels.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Creates carbonation in fizzy drinks. Also used as a packaging gas to extend freshness.

ingredients.name: polysorbate 60
ingredients.explanation: Synthetic emulsifier in baked goods and creams. Animal studies showed organ weight changes.
ingredients.notes: CSPI rates Caution. Same family as polysorbate 80. JECFA ADI established.

ingredients.name: polysorbate 20
ingredients.explanation: Synthetic emulsifier used in desserts and salad dressings. Same concerns as polysorbate 80.
ingredients.notes: CSPI rates Caution. Part of polysorbate family. Gut microbiome disruption studied in animals.

ingredients.name: polysorbate 65
ingredients.explanation: Synthetic emulsifier used in ice cream and whipped toppings. Similar concerns to other polysorbates.
ingredients.notes: JECFA ADI established. Less commonly used than polysorbate 60 or 80.

ingredients.name: datem
aliases: diacetyl tartaric acid esters of mono and diglycerides
ingredients.explanation: Synthetic emulsifier used in bread to improve dough strength. Some heart-related concerns in animals.
ingredients.notes: CSPI rates Caution. Animal study showed enlarged hearts at high doses. Human risk at food levels unclear.

ingredients.name: carboxymethyl cellulose
ingredients.explanation: Synthetic cellulose used in ice cream and sauces. May disrupt gut microbiome at high intake.
ingredients.notes: CSPI rates Caution. 2015 mouse study showed gut inflammation at doses above normal food intake.

ingredients.name: hydroxypropyl methylcellulose
ingredients.explanation: Modified cellulose used in plant-based foods and sauces. Not absorbed by the body.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Used as a fat replacer in reduced-fat foods. Common in tablet coatings too.

ingredients.name: acetylated distarch phosphate
ingredients.explanation: Chemically modified starch for stable thickening in frozen foods. Well-reviewed.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. JECFA reviewed. Used in baby foods and frozen meals. Considered safe at normal levels.

ingredients.name: hydroxypropyl distarch phosphate
ingredients.explanation: Modified starch that stays stable during heating and cooling. Safe at food use levels.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Widely used in sauces, gravies, and yogurts. Resistant to breakdown during cooking.

ingredients.name: sorbitan monostearate
ingredients.explanation: Emulsifier made from sorbitol and stearic acid. Well-studied and widely permitted.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. JECFA ADI set. Common in cake mixes and chocolate coatings.

ingredients.name: sorbitan tristearate
ingredients.explanation: Sorbitan-based emulsifier used in chocolate and coatings. Safe at normal food levels.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Used to control fat bloom in chocolate. JECFA reviewed and approved.

ingredients.name: sorbitan monolaurate
ingredients.explanation: Emulsifier from sorbitol and lauric acid. Used in yeast foods and dressings. Safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Less commonly used than other span emulsifiers. Well within safety limits.

ingredients.name: glycerol
ingredients.explanation: Natural compound found in all fats. Used to keep foods moist. Completely safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Naturally produced during fat digestion in the body. Also used in medicines and cosmetics.

ingredients.name: propylene glycol
ingredients.explanation: Synthetic humectant and solvent. Generally safe but banned in cat food due to toxicity to cats.
ingredients.notes: GRAS for humans. CSPI rates Caution. EU restricts use to specific food categories.

ingredients.name: lactic acid esters of monoglycerides
ingredients.display_name: Lactic Acid Esters of Mono and Diglycerides
ingredients.explanation: Emulsifier from lactic acid and monoglycerides. Used in bread and desserts. Safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Natural-derived components. Widely used in the baking industry.

ingredients.name: citric acid esters of monoglycerides
ingredients.display_name: Citric Acid Esters of Mono and Diglycerides
ingredients.explanation: Emulsifier from citric acid and monoglycerides. Used in margarine and pate. Safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Used to improve texture and shelf life. Derived from natural components.

ingredients.name: acetic acid esters of monoglycerides
ingredients.display_name: Acetic Acid Esters of Mono and Diglycerides
ingredients.explanation: Emulsifier made from acetic acid and fats. Used in whipped toppings. Safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Part of the mono and diglyceride ester family. Used in aerosol whipped cream.

ingredients.name: sucrose esters of fatty acids
ingredients.explanation: Emulsifiers made from sugar and fatty acids. Natural-derived and well-tolerated.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. JECFA ADI established. Used in bread, dairy, and infant formula.

ingredients.name: sucroglycerides
ingredients.explanation: Mixture of sucrose esters and monoglycerides. Gentle emulsifier. Safe at normal use.
ingredients.notes: JECFA reviewed. Less commonly used. Found in some margarines and ice cream.

ingredients.name: polyglycerol esters of fatty acids
ingredients.explanation: Emulsifiers made from glycerol and fatty acids. Used in cakes and chocolate. Safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. JECFA ADI set. Widely used in the confectionery and baking industries.

ingredients.name: polyglycerol polyricinoleate
ingredients.explanation: Cheap emulsifier used in chocolate to replace cocoa butter. Safe but controversial.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Derived from castor oil. CSPI rates Safe. Very commonly used in compound chocolate.

ingredients.name: propylene glycol esters of fatty acids
ingredients.display_name: Propylene Glycol Esters of Fatty Acids
ingredients.explanation: Emulsifier used in cake mixes and whipped toppings. Well-studied and safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. JECFA reviewed. Used to improve aeration and texture in baked products.

ingredients.name: stearoyl tartrate
ingredients.explanation: Dough conditioner and emulsifier used in bread. Safe at normal food use levels.
ingredients.notes: JECFA reviewed. Strengthens dough structure. Contributes to bread volume and texture.

ingredients.name: calcium stearoyl lactylate
ingredients.explanation: Dough conditioner used in bread. Calcium version of SSL. Safe and well-studied.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Works similarly to sodium stearoyl lactylate. Used in bread and bakery products.

ingredients.name: gum arabic
ingredients.explanation: Natural tree gum from acacia plants. Used to stabilize soft drinks and confectionery.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. One of the oldest food additives known. JECFA reviewed extensively. No known concerns.

ingredients.name: arabic gum spray dried
ingredients.explanation: Processed form of gum arabic. Same safety profile. Used in flavor encapsulation.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Used in powdered flavor coatings and beverage emulsions. Identical safety to e414.

ingredients.name: tragacanth gum
ingredients.explanation: Natural plant gum from thorny shrubs. Used to stabilize salad dressings. Very safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. One of the oldest food thickeners in use. Very low use levels needed.

ingredients.name: pectins
ingredients.explanation: Natural fiber from fruit peels used to set jams and gels. Excellent safety record.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Pectin is also a beneficial dietary fiber. Widely used in jams, jellies, and yogurts.

ingredients.name: oxidatively polymerized soybean oil
ingredients.explanation: Starch treated with oxidizing agents for better texture in food products. Safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Used in paper coatings too. JECFA reviewed. No adverse effects at food use levels.

ingredients.name: starch acetate
ingredients.explanation: Acetylated starch for better freeze-thaw stability in sauces. Safe and well-reviewed.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Prevents starch retrogradation in frozen foods. JECFA reviewed.

ingredients.name: distarch phosphate
ingredients.explanation: Cross-linked starch for heat and acid stability. Used in canned soups and gravies.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. JECFA reviewed. Very stable under heat and acidic conditions.

ingredients.name: sodium acid pyrophosphate
ingredients.explanation: Leavening acid used in baking powder and pancake mixes. Safe at normal food levels.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Most widely used leavening acid in the US. High phosphate intake from multiple sources should be watched by kidney patients.

ingredients.name: monocalcium phosphate
ingredients.explanation: Leavening acid and calcium source used in baking powder. Safe and well-studied.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Also adds calcium to food. Common in self-rising flour and baking powder.

ingredients.name: dicalcium phosphate
ingredients.explanation: Calcium and phosphorus supplement used in cereals and toothpaste. Very safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Used to fortify cereals and flour with calcium. Also used in antacids.

ingredients.name: tricalcium phosphate
ingredients.explanation: Anti-caking agent and calcium supplement in powders and spices. Very safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Used in powdered spices and dry mixes to prevent clumping. Also a calcium supplement.

ingredients.name: sodium hexametaphosphate
ingredients.explanation: Sequestrant used in seafood and dairy to retain moisture. High phosphate intake is a concern.
ingredients.notes: GRAS but high cumulative phosphate from multiple food sources is a concern for kidney health.

ingredients.name: tetrasodium pyrophosphate
ingredients.explanation: Phosphate used in marshmallows and processed cheese. Excess phosphate burdens kidneys.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Common in processed cheese and instant noodles. Kidney patients should limit phosphate intake.

ingredients.name: potassium pyrophosphate
ingredients.explanation: Phosphate used as an emulsifying salt in processed foods. Safe at normal food levels.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Used in processed cheese and surimi. Lower risk profile than sodium phosphates.

ingredients.name: magnesium stearate
ingredients.explanation: Magnesium salt used as a lubricant in supplements and tablets. Safe at food levels.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Very commonly used in dietary supplements. No safety concerns at typical intake.

ingredients.name: calcium silicate
ingredients.explanation: Natural mineral used as anti-caking agent in table salt and powders. Very safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Used in salt, baking powder, and dry mixes. No known health concerns.

ingredients.name: magnesium silicate
ingredients.explanation: Mineral anti-caking agent used in rice and powders. Safe at food use levels.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Food-grade talc is different from cosmetic talc. No asbestos contamination concern in food grade.

ingredients.name: sodium ferrocyanide
ingredients.explanation: Iron-cyanide compound used in table salt to prevent clumping. Tightly bound cyanide is safe.
ingredients.notes: The cyanide is chemically bound and cannot be released under normal conditions. JECFA reviewed and approved.

ingredients.name: potassium ferrocyanide
ingredients.explanation: Used in wine and salt processing to remove metals. Cyanide is tightly bound and stable.
ingredients.notes: JECFA ADI established. Very low use levels. Cyanide does not release under normal food conditions.

ingredients.name: hydrogen peroxide
ingredients.explanation: Used to bleach flour and sterilize food equipment. Fully decomposes before consumption.
ingredients.notes: GRAS as a processing aid. Breaks down to water and oxygen. No residue remains in final food.

ingredients.name: benzoyl peroxide
ingredients.explanation: Chemical bleaching agent for flour. Banned in EU and China but used in US and India.
ingredients.notes: EU banned it. US FDA allows up to 40 ppm. Converts to benzoic acid in flour. CSPI rates Caution.

ingredients.name: chlorine
ingredients.explanation: Used to bleach and age cake flour in the US. Banned in EU for flour treatment.
ingredients.notes: CSPI rates Caution. EU banned for flour use. Residue levels in finished flour are low.

ingredients.name: l-cysteine
ingredients.explanation: Amino acid used to soften dough and reduce mixing time. Often derived from hair or feathers.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Source may be animal-derived (duck feathers, human hair) or synthetic. Vegan versions available.

ingredients.name: ascorbic acid flour treatment
ingredients.explanation: Vitamin C used as a dough improver in bread making. Completely safe and beneficial.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Strengthens gluten network in dough. One of the safest flour improvers available.

ingredients.name: amylase
ingredients.explanation: Enzyme that breaks down starch into sugars. Naturally in saliva. Used in bread making.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Naturally present in the body. Used to improve bread texture and extend shelf life.

ingredients.name: protease
ingredients.explanation: Protein-digesting enzyme used in meat tenderizers and bread. Naturally occurring.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Papain comes from papaya, bromelain from pineapple. Used in meat processing and baking.

ingredients.name: lipase
ingredients.explanation: Fat-digesting enzyme used to develop flavor in cheese. Safe and naturally occurring.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Naturally present in the body. Used in cheese ripening and flavor development.

ingredients.name: transglutaminase
ingredients.explanation: Enzyme that binds proteins together. Used to reshape meat scraps. Food safety concerns.
ingredients.notes: CSPI rates Caution. EU has not approved it for direct food use. Concern that it hides poor-quality meat.

ingredients.name: invertase
ingredients.explanation: Enzyme that splits sucrose into glucose and fructose. Used in chocolate fillings. Safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Creates soft creamy centers in chocolate candy. Naturally found in yeast and honey bees.

ingredients.name: tannins
ingredients.explanation: Plant-derived compounds used in wine clarification. Naturally in tea and grapes. Safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Used as a fining agent in wine and beer. Very high doses may reduce iron absorption.

ingredients.name: activated carbon
ingredients.explanation: Food-grade charcoal used to decolorize liquids and filter impurities. Safe in food.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Used in sugar refining and spirits production. Trendy in black-colored foods.

ingredients.name: bentonite
ingredients.explanation: Natural clay used to clarify wine and remove proteins. Not in the final product.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Used as a processing aid only, not a food additive. Removed before bottling.

ingredients.name: diatomaceous earth
ingredients.explanation: Natural silica from fossilized algae used as a filter aid in brewing. Not consumed.
ingredients.notes: GRAS as a processing/filter aid. Removed before the product reaches the consumer.

ingredients.name: isinglass
ingredients.explanation: Fining agent from fish bladders used to clarify beer and wine. Fish allergen concern.
ingredients.notes: Not vegan. Fish-allergic individuals should note it may leave trace residues in beverages.

ingredients.name: mono sodium phosphate
ingredients.explanation: Phosphate salt used to control acidity in processed foods. Safe at normal levels.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Used in evaporated milk and processed cheese. Kidney patients should monitor total phosphate.

ingredients.name: glucoamylase
ingredients.explanation: Enzyme used in brewing and sweetener production to convert starch to glucose. Very safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Used in distilling, brewing, and high-fructose corn syrup production. No concerns.

ingredients.name: pectinase
ingredients.explanation: Enzyme that breaks down pectin in fruit juice processing. Improves juice clarity.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Used in wine, juice, and jam production. Naturally found in many plants and microorganisms.

ingredients.name: cellulase
ingredients.explanation: Enzyme that breaks down plant cell walls. Used to improve texture in plant-based foods.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Humans do not naturally produce cellulase. Derived from fungi. No known concerns.

ingredients.name: laccase
ingredients.explanation: Enzyme used to remove oxygen in wine and juice to prevent browning. Natural and safe.
ingredients.notes: EFSA reviewing enzyme panel approvals. Generally regarded as safe from fungal or plant sources.

ingredients.name: almonds
ingredients.explanation: Nutrient-dense tree nut rich in healthy fats, vitamin E, and magnesium. Very safe.
ingredients.notes: Major allergen. Must be declared on food labels in US, EU, and India. Raw and roasted both safe.

ingredients.name: cashews
ingredients.explanation: Tree nut with healthy fats and protein. Safe for most people. Common allergen.
ingredients.notes: Major allergen in many countries. Raw cashews contain urushiol in the shell, removed during processing.

ingredients.name: walnuts
ingredients.explanation: Rich in omega-3 fatty acids and antioxidants. Excellent brain health food. Safe.
ingredients.notes: Major tree nut allergen. Highest omega-3 content among all nuts. Declared allergen in EU and US.

ingredients.name: peanuts
ingredients.explanation: Technically a legume. Nutrient-rich and widely consumed. Strongest food allergen known.
ingredients.notes: Top 9 major allergen in the US. Can cause severe anaphylaxis. Mandatory labeling worldwide.

ingredients.name: pistachios
ingredients.explanation: Tree nut with high protein and antioxidants. Safe and nutritious for most people.
ingredients.notes: Major tree nut allergen. Aflatoxin contamination possible if poorly stored. Buy from reputable sources.

ingredients.name: hazelnuts
ingredients.explanation: Tree nut used in confectionery and spreads. Rich in vitamin E. Common allergen.
ingredients.notes: Major allergen in EU. Cross-reactive with birch pollen allergy. Common in chocolate products.

ingredients.name: sesame seeds
ingredients.explanation: Tiny seeds packed with healthy fats, calcium, and lignans. Safe and nutritious.
ingredients.notes: Newly added as 9th major allergen in the US (2023). Must now be declared on food labels.

ingredients.name: flaxseeds
ingredients.explanation: Rich in omega-3 and fiber. Raw seeds contain small amounts of cyanogenic compounds.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Normal food quantities are safe. Raw seeds have trace cyanogenic glycosides, neutralized by cooking.

ingredients.name: chia seeds
ingredients.explanation: High in omega-3, fiber, and calcium. Absorbs water rapidly. Safe for most people.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Choking risk if consumed dry without water. Novel food status in EU approved 2009.

ingredients.name: sunflower seeds
ingredients.explanation: Rich in vitamin E and healthy fats. Widely used in snacks and baking. Very safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Sunflower allergy is rare but exists. High in linoleic acid (omega-6).

ingredients.name: pumpkin seeds
ingredients.explanation: Rich in magnesium, zinc, and healthy fats. Used in snacks and toppings. Very safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Good source of plant-based zinc. Also used in traditional medicine for prostate health.

ingredients.name: oats
ingredients.explanation: Whole grain rich in beta-glucan fiber. Naturally gluten-free but often cross-contaminated.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Celiac patients must use certified gluten-free oats to avoid wheat cross-contamination.

ingredients.name: barley
ingredients.explanation: Ancient grain with high fiber and beta-glucan. Contains gluten. Safe for most people.
ingredients.notes: Contains gluten. Not suitable for celiac patients. Rich in soluble fiber. Used in soups and beer.

ingredients.name: millet
ingredients.explanation: Gluten-free ancient grains widely used in India. Rich in iron and fiber. Very safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Includes bajra, jowar, ragi. Goitrogenic compounds present but not a concern at normal intake.

ingredients.name: quinoa
ingredients.explanation: Gluten-free pseudo-cereal with complete protein. Safe and highly nutritious.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Contains saponins on the outer coat. Rinse before cooking to remove bitter taste.

ingredients.name: maize starch
ingredients.explanation: Pure starch from corn. Gluten-free. Widely used as a thickener and coating. Safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. One of the most commonly used food starches globally. Mostly derived from GMO corn in the US.

ingredients.name: orange
ingredients.explanation: Citrus fruit rich in vitamin C and flavonoids. Safe and widely consumed.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Peel wax coatings on commercial oranges may contain food-grade wax or fungicide treatments.

ingredients.name: mango
ingredients.explanation: Tropical fruit rich in vitamins A and C. Popular in Indian cuisine. Very safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Mango skin contains urushiol, same compound as poison ivy. Flesh is completely safe.

ingredients.name: banana
ingredients.explanation: Rich in potassium, B6, and natural sugars. Highly digestible and safe for all ages.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Latex-fruit syndrome: people with latex allergy may react to banana. High natural sugar content.

ingredients.name: apple
ingredients.explanation: Rich in fiber, vitamin C, and antioxidants. One of the most widely eaten fruits. Safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Seeds contain amygdalin which releases cyanide, but amounts in normal eating are harmless.

ingredients.name: dates
ingredients.explanation: High-sugar dried fruit with fiber, potassium, and antioxidants. Safe in moderation.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Very high sugar content. Diabetics should monitor portion size. Natural sweetener alternative.

ingredients.name: spinach
ingredients.explanation: Leafy green rich in iron, folate, and vitamins K and A. Very nutritious and safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. High in oxalates. Kidney stone patients should moderate intake. Vitamin K may interact with warfarin.

ingredients.name: carrot
ingredients.explanation: Rich in beta-carotene and fiber. Excellent for eye health. Very safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Excessive consumption can cause carotenemia (skin yellowing), which is harmless.

ingredients.name: potato starch
ingredients.explanation: Starch extracted from potatoes. Gluten-free thickener. Very safe and widely used.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. One of the cleanest starches available. Resistant starch content has prebiotic benefits.

ingredients.name: cardamom
ingredients.explanation: Aromatic spice used in sweets and chai. Rich in antioxidants. Very safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Popular in Indian, Middle Eastern, and Scandinavian cuisine. No known safety concerns.

ingredients.name: cloves
ingredients.explanation: Spice with eugenol as active compound. Safe in food quantities. Antiseptic properties.
ingredients.notes: GRAS at food use levels. Clove oil in large amounts can be toxic. Normal cooking use is safe.

ingredients.name: bay leaf
ingredients.explanation: Aromatic herb used in cooking. Adds flavor to curries and stews. Very safe to consume.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Leaves are usually removed before eating. Indian bay leaf is a different species than European.

ingredients.name: star anise
ingredients.explanation: Star-shaped spice used in biryani and Chinese cooking. Rich in anethole. Safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Do not confuse with Japanese star anise which is toxic. Food-grade star anise is completely safe.

ingredients.name: fenugreek
ingredients.explanation: Seeds and leaves used widely in Indian cooking. May help blood sugar levels.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. May lower blood sugar levels. Diabetics on medication should monitor. Common in Indian food.

ingredients.name: black cumin
ingredients.explanation: Small black seeds used in Indian and Middle Eastern cooking. Rich in thymoquinone.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Not to be confused with black caraway. Popular in naan bread and pickles. Safe at food levels.

ingredients.name: mace
ingredients.explanation: Red aril covering of nutmeg. Similar flavor, used in biryanis and sweets. Safe at food levels.
ingredients.notes: GRAS at normal food amounts. Like nutmeg, large doses can cause hallucinations. Cooking amounts are safe.

ingredients.name: nutmeg
ingredients.explanation: Warm aromatic spice used in desserts and biryanis. Safe in normal food quantities.
ingredients.notes: GRAS at culinary doses. Large amounts (over 5g) can cause myristicin toxicity. Normal cooking is safe.

ingredients.name: dried mango powder
ingredients.explanation: Tangy powder from dried unripe mango. Used as a souring agent in Indian cooking.
ingredients.notes: FSSAI approved. Natural souring agent. Popular in chaat, curries, and marinades. No safety concerns.

ingredients.name: pomegranate seeds
ingredients.explanation: Dried pomegranate seeds used as a souring spice in Indian cooking. Rich in antioxidants.
ingredients.notes: FSSAI approved. Used in chutneys and curries. Pomegranate juice may interact with some medications.

ingredients.name: tamarind
ingredients.explanation: Tangy pod fruit used in chutneys, curries, and rasam. Rich in tartaric acid. Very safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. One of the most widely used souring agents in South Indian and Southeast Asian cooking. No concerns.

ingredients.name: kokum
ingredients.explanation: Dried fruit rind used as a souring agent in Konkani and Goan cooking. Very safe.
ingredients.notes: FSSAI approved. Used in fish curries and kokum sherbets. Contains hydroxycitric acid. No known concerns.

ingredients.name: raw mango
ingredients.explanation: Unripe mango used fresh or dried for its tangy flavor. Rich in vitamin C. Safe.
ingredients.notes: FSSAI approved. Used in pickles, chutneys, and drinks. Contains oxalic acid in small amounts.

ingredients.name: jaggery
ingredients.explanation: Unrefined sugar from sugarcane or palm sap. Contains minerals and molasses. Safe.
ingredients.notes: FSSAI approved. Slightly more nutritious than refined sugar. Still high in sugar. Diabetics should limit.

ingredients.name: palm sugar
ingredients.explanation: Natural sweetener from palm tree sap. Lower glycemic index than white sugar.
ingredients.notes: FSSAI approved. Popular in South Indian and Bengali sweets. Still a sugar. Monitor intake for diabetes.

ingredients.name: mishri
ingredients.explanation: Large sugar crystals used in Indian sweets and paan. Essentially pure sucrose. Safe.
ingredients.notes: FSSAI approved. Used in religious offerings and as a mouth freshener. Same as refined sugar nutritionally.

ingredients.name: mustard oil
ingredients.explanation: Common cooking oil in North India. Contains erucic acid which raises heart concerns.
ingredients.notes: FDA restricts for cooking use in the US due to erucic acid. FSSAI allows in India. High erucic acid content.

ingredients.name: sesame oil
ingredients.explanation: Cold-pressed or refined oil from sesame seeds. Rich in antioxidants. Very safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Sesame allergy applies here too. Widely used in South Indian and Chinese cooking.

ingredients.name: groundnut oil
ingredients.explanation: Oil from pressed peanuts. High smoke point. Common in Indian cooking. Safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Refined groundnut oil is generally safe even for those with peanut allergies. Check labels carefully.

ingredients.name: paneer
ingredients.explanation: Fresh unaged cheese made by curdling milk. High in protein and calcium. Safe.
ingredients.notes: FSSAI has standards for fat content in paneer. Not suitable for those with lactose intolerance or dairy allergy.

ingredients.name: curd
ingredients.explanation: Fermented milk with live cultures. Excellent probiotic food. Safe for most people.
ingredients.notes: FSSAI approved. Contains lactobacillus cultures. Lower lactose than milk. Good for gut health.

ingredients.name: khoya
ingredients.explanation: Milk reduced by slow cooking until semi-solid. Used in Indian sweets. Safe.
ingredients.notes: FSSAI regulated. Adulteration with starch or fat is a common market concern. Buy from trusted sources.

ingredients.name: besan
ingredients.explanation: Flour from ground chana dal. High protein and gluten-free. Widely used in Indian cooking.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Chickpea allergy is rare but exists. Used in pakoras, kadhi, and ladoos.

ingredients.name: suji
ingredients.explanation: Coarsely ground durum wheat used in upma, halwa, and idli. Contains gluten.
ingredients.notes: FSSAI approved. Contains gluten. Not suitable for celiac patients. One of India's most used grains.

ingredients.name: poha
ingredients.explanation: Flattened parboiled rice used for quick Indian breakfast dishes. Light and easy to digest.
ingredients.notes: FSSAI approved. Gluten-free. One of the most popular breakfast ingredients across India.

ingredients.name: sabudana
ingredients.explanation: Starch balls from tapioca root. Gluten-free. Used in fasting foods across India.
ingredients.notes: FSSAI approved. Almost pure starch with minimal nutrients. Soaking required before cooking.

ingredients.name: chana dal
ingredients.explanation: Split chickpeas rich in protein and fiber. Key ingredient in Indian cooking. Very safe.
ingredients.notes: FSSAI approved. Contains antinutrients like phytic acid that are reduced by soaking and cooking.

ingredients.name: urad dal
ingredients.explanation: High-protein lentil used in idli, dosa batter and dal makhani. Safe and nutritious.
ingredients.notes: FSSAI approved. High in purines. Gout patients should limit intake. Essential for South Indian cuisine.

ingredients.name: toor dal
ingredients.explanation: Most commonly used dal in India. Base of sambar and many dals. Protein-rich. Safe.
ingredients.notes: FSSAI approved. Adulteration with kesari dal (lathyrus sativus) is a concern in India. Buy quality sources.

ingredients.name: moong dal
ingredients.explanation: One of the most easily digestible legumes. Used in khichdi and sprouts. Very safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Excellent for babies and the elderly. Low antinutrient content. Used in Ayurvedic cooking.

ingredients.name: asafoetida
ingredients.explanation: Pungent resin used as an onion-garlic substitute. Anti-flatulent. Safe in food amounts.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Commercial hing is mixed with wheat flour. Celiac patients should check for wheat-free hing.

ingredients.name: curry leaves
ingredients.explanation: Aromatic leaves used for tempering in South Indian cooking. Rich in antioxidants.
ingredients.notes: FSSAI approved. Not the same as curry powder. Fresh or dried leaves used in tadka across India.

ingredients.name: amla
ingredients.explanation: Vitamin C-rich Indian fruit used in pickles, chutneys, and Ayurvedic medicine. Very safe.
ingredients.notes: FSSAI approved. One of the richest natural sources of vitamin C. Used extensively in Ayurveda.

ingredients.name: moringa
ingredients.explanation: Highly nutritious drumstick tree. Leaves and pods used widely in South Indian cooking.
ingredients.notes: FSSAI approved. Moringa root and root bark contain toxic alkaloids. Leaves and pods are safe to eat.

ingredients.name: chaat masala
ingredients.explanation: Tangy spice blend with amchur, black salt, and cumin. Used as a finishing spice mix.
ingredients.notes: FSSAI regulated as a spice blend. Contains black salt and dried mango powder. High sodium content.

ingredients.name: black salt
ingredients.explanation: Volcanic rock salt with sulfurous flavor. Used in chaat and raita. Safe in food amounts.
ingredients.notes: FSSAI approved. High sodium like regular salt. Contains trace iron sulfide. Distinctive egg-like aroma.

ingredients.name: garam masala
ingredients.explanation: Aromatic blend of warm spices like cinnamon, cloves, and cardamom. Very safe.
ingredients.notes: FSSAI regulated as a spice blend. Recipe varies by region. All component spices are individually safe.

ingredients.name: rose water
ingredients.explanation: Distilled rose petal water used in Indian sweets and desserts. Safe at food use levels.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Used in gulab jamun, kheer, and biryanis. Very low concentration of rose compounds.

ingredients.name: kewra water
ingredients.explanation: Floral essence from screwpine flowers used in biryani and sweets. Safe at food levels.
ingredients.notes: FSSAI approved. Distinctive North Indian flavor. Used in biryani, gulab jamun, and mutton dishes.

ingredients.name: saffron
ingredients.explanation: World's most expensive spice. Provides golden color and unique flavor. Safe at culinary doses.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Adulteration is common. Very large doses (above 5g) can be toxic. Culinary amounts are safe.

ingredients.name: kokum butter
ingredients.explanation: Solid fat extracted from kokum seeds. Used in chocolates and cosmetics. Safe.
ingredients.notes: FSSAI approved. Natural cocoa butter alternative. Used in premium chocolates and confectionery.

ingredients.name: neem
ingredients.explanation: Bitter herb used medicinally. Neem leaves eaten in small amounts. High doses are toxic.
ingredients.notes: Neem oil is not for food use. Small amounts of neem leaves in cooking are a traditional Indian practice only.

ingredients.name: casein
ingredients.explanation: Main protein in milk. Used in protein powders and processed cheese. Safe for non-dairy-allergic.
ingredients.notes: Major milk allergen. Must be declared on labels. Not suitable for milk allergy or vegan diets.

ingredients.name: lactalbumin
ingredients.explanation: Whey protein fraction from milk. Used in infant formula and sports foods. Safe.
ingredients.notes: Major milk allergen. Key protein in human breast milk. Used in infant formula to mimic breast milk composition.

ingredients.name: lactoglobulin
ingredients.explanation: Most abundant whey protein. Not present in human milk. Common trigger for milk allergy.
ingredients.notes: Major cow milk allergen. Absent in human breast milk. Heat-stable but partially denatured by pasteurization.

ingredients.name: lactose
ingredients.explanation: Natural sugar in milk. Causes bloating and discomfort in lactose-intolerant people.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. About 70% of the world's population has some degree of lactose intolerance. Must be declared.

ingredients.name: gluten
ingredients.explanation: Protein complex in wheat, barley, and rye. Causes serious disease in celiac patients.
ingredients.notes: Major allergen. Triggers celiac disease, wheat allergy, and non-celiac gluten sensitivity. Mandatory labeling globally.

ingredients.name: gliadin
ingredients.explanation: Gluten component that triggers celiac disease. Present in wheat, rye, and barley.
ingredients.notes: The specific fraction of gluten responsible for celiac damage. Triggers immune response in celiac patients.

ingredients.name: wheat starch
ingredients.explanation: Starch from wheat. May contain trace gluten. Risk for celiac patients even in small amounts.
ingredients.notes: Celiac-safe only if labeled as specially processed to remove gluten below 20ppm. Otherwise risky for celiacs.

ingredients.name: egg albumin
ingredients.explanation: Main protein in egg whites. Used in meringues, foams, and protein powders. Safe.
ingredients.notes: Major egg allergen. Must be declared on labels. Raw egg white contains avidin which blocks biotin absorption.

ingredients.name: egg yolk powder
ingredients.explanation: Dehydrated egg yolk used as an emulsifier and enriching agent. Safe.
ingredients.notes: Major egg allergen. Used in mayonnaise, pasta, and bakery products. Rich in lecithin and fat-soluble vitamins.

ingredients.name: ovomucoid
ingredients.explanation: Heat-resistant egg white protein. The main allergen that persists even after cooking.
ingredients.notes: Most potent egg allergen. Heat-stable meaning baked egg products can still trigger reactions in egg-allergic people.

ingredients.name: fish gelatin
ingredients.explanation: Gelatin from fish skin and bones. Alternative to pork gelatin. Fish allergen concern.
ingredients.notes: Major fish allergen. Must be declared. Popular in halal and kosher products as pork gelatin alternative.

ingredients.name: shellfish extract
ingredients.explanation: Flavor extract from crustaceans like shrimp and crab. Potent allergen. Declare always.
ingredients.notes: Major allergen in US, EU, and India. Can cause severe anaphylaxis. Mandatory labeling globally.

ingredients.name: fish sauce
ingredients.explanation: Fermented fish liquid used as a condiment in Asian cooking. Safe but a fish allergen.
ingredients.notes: Major fish allergen. High in sodium. Must be declared as containing fish on labels.

ingredients.name: tropomyosin
ingredients.explanation: Main protein allergen in shrimp and crustaceans. Heat-stable and hard to eliminate.
ingredients.notes: Primary allergen in shellfish allergy. Highly heat-stable. Cannot be destroyed by cooking.

ingredients.name: parvalbumin
ingredients.explanation: Main protein responsible for fish allergy. Present in most fish species. Heat-stable.
ingredients.notes: Primary fish allergen. Cross-reactive across many fish species. Heat-stable, survives cooking.

ingredients.name: textured vegetable protein
ingredients.explanation: Defatted soy flour made into meat-like chunks. Popular vegetarian protein. Safe.
ingredients.notes: Major soy allergen. Extremely popular in India as a meat substitute. FSSAI regulates fat content.

ingredients.name: almond flour
ingredients.explanation: Blanched ground almonds used in gluten-free baking. Nutritious and safe.
ingredients.notes: Major tree nut allergen. Must be declared. High in fat and protein. Popular in low-carb baking.

ingredients.name: coconut
ingredients.explanation: Versatile tropical fruit used in oil, milk, flour, and fresh form. Widely safe.
ingredients.notes: FDA classifies as a tree nut allergen. Coconut allergy is rare. High in saturated fat.

ingredients.name: coconut milk
ingredients.explanation: Liquid extracted from coconut flesh. Lactose-free dairy alternative. Safe for most.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Tree nut allergen declaration required in some regions. High in saturated fat.

ingredients.name: lupin flour
ingredients.explanation: High-protein legume flour used in gluten-free baking. Cross-reacts with peanut allergy.
ingredients.notes: Major allergen in EU. People with peanut allergy have up to 30% chance of lupin cross-reaction.

ingredients.name: mustard protein
ingredients.explanation: Allergenic proteins from mustard seeds. Can cause severe reactions in sensitized people.
ingredients.notes: Major allergen in EU and Canada. Must be declared. Mustard allergy can cause anaphylaxis.

ingredients.name: celery
ingredients.explanation: Low-calorie vegetable used in soups and salads. Major allergen in Europe.
ingredients.notes: Major allergen in EU. Not on the US top 9 list. Can cross-react with birch pollen allergy.

ingredients.name: sulphur dioxide
ingredients.explanation: Gas form of sulfites used in wine and dried fruit. Triggers asthma and allergic reactions.
ingredients.notes: Major allergen group. Must be declared when above 10ppm in EU and US. Asthmatics especially sensitive.

ingredients.name: collagen
ingredients.explanation: Structural protein from animal connective tissue. Used in supplements and food. Safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Usually derived from bovine or porcine sources. Not vegan. Fish-sourced versions also available.

ingredients.name: pea protein
ingredients.explanation: Plant protein from yellow peas. Popular vegan protein source. Very safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Pea allergy is rare. One of the cleanest plant proteins. Used widely in vegan food products.

ingredients.name: rice protein
ingredients.explanation: Hypoallergenic plant protein from rice. One of the least allergenic proteins available.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Rice allergy is very rare. Popular in baby food and hypoallergenic diets.

ingredients.name: hemp protein
ingredients.explanation: Complete plant protein from hemp seeds. Contains omega-3 fatty acids. Safe and legal.
ingredients.notes: GRAS in US and EU. Negligible THC content. India has restrictions on hemp food products.

ingredients.name: spirulina
ingredients.explanation: Protein-rich blue-green algae used as a supplement and natural color. Safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. FSSAI approved. Wild-harvested spirulina may contain toxins. Only use from certified sources.

ingredients.name: chlorella
ingredients.explanation: Single-celled green algae rich in protein and chlorophyll. Safe as a food supplement.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Cell wall must be broken to be digestible. Source quality matters. No concerns at food levels.

ingredients.name: insect protein
ingredients.explanation: Emerging protein from edible insects. Cross-reacts with shellfish allergy. Not yet widely regulated.
ingredients.notes: EFSA has approved several insect species for food use. Shellfish-allergic individuals may react. Labeling required in EU.

ingredients.name: maple syrup
ingredients.explanation: Natural sweetener from maple tree sap. Contains trace minerals and antioxidants. Safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Mostly sucrose and water. Grade A is most common. Adulteration with corn syrup is a market concern.

ingredients.name: agave syrup
ingredients.explanation: High-fructose sweetener from agave plant. Marketed as healthy but very high in fructose.
ingredients.notes: CSPI rates Caution. Up to 90% fructose content. Excess fructose linked to fatty liver and metabolic issues.

ingredients.name: monk fruit extract
ingredients.explanation: Natural zero-calorie sweetener from monk fruit. 200 times sweeter than sugar. Very safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. No known safety concerns. Increasingly popular as a natural alternative to artificial sweeteners.

ingredients.name: thaumatin
ingredients.explanation: Protein-based sweetener from West African katemfe fruit. 2000 times sweeter than sugar.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Natural protein. JECFA ADI not specified meaning safe at any food use level. Rare in Indian foods.

ingredients.name: maltitol
ingredients.explanation: Sugar alcohol with 75% of sugar's sweetness. Causes digestive distress in large amounts.
ingredients.notes: Laxative effect warning required in EU when above 10% in product. Not calorie-free. Raises blood sugar moderately.

ingredients.name: isomalt
ingredients.explanation: Sugar alcohol used in sugar-free candy and diabetic foods. Very low glycemic impact.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Used in hard candy and chewing gum. Laxative effect possible at high intake. Tooth-friendly.

ingredients.name: lactitol
ingredients.explanation: Sugar alcohol from lactose used in diabetic and low-calorie foods. Acts as a prebiotic.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Also used medically as a laxative. Provides some prebiotic benefit. Not suitable for milk allergy.

ingredients.name: vitamin d
ingredients.explanation: Fat-soluble vitamin essential for bone health. Added to milk and cereals. Safe at normal levels.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Deficiency is extremely common in India. Toxicity possible at very high supplement doses. Food levels are safe.

ingredients.name: vitamin a
ingredients.explanation: Fat-soluble vitamin essential for vision and immunity. Added to fortified foods. Safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. High dose supplements can be toxic. Food fortification levels are safe. Pregnant women should not overdose.

ingredients.name: vitamin b12
ingredients.explanation: Essential vitamin for nerve health and blood cells. Deficiency common in vegetarians.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Critical nutrient for vegans and vegetarians who are at high risk of deficiency. No toxicity risk.

ingredients.name: zinc
ingredients.explanation: Essential mineral for immunity and wound healing. Added to cereals and supplements.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. High doses from supplements can cause nausea and copper deficiency. Food levels are safe.

ingredients.name: magnesium
ingredients.explanation: Essential mineral for muscle and nerve function. Added to fortified foods. Very safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Deficiency is common. High supplemental doses cause loose stools. Food fortification levels are safe.

ingredients.name: iodine
ingredients.explanation: Essential mineral added to salt to prevent thyroid disorders. Critically important nutrient.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Mandatory iodization of salt in India under FSSAI. Both deficiency and excess can affect thyroid function.

ingredients.name: selenium
ingredients.explanation: Trace mineral with antioxidant properties. Small window between deficiency and toxicity.
ingredients.notes: GRAS at food levels. Upper limit is 400 mcg per day. Indian soils are selenium-deficient. Used in functional foods.

ingredients.name: aflatoxin
ingredients.explanation: Mold toxin found in poorly stored peanuts, corn, and spices. Potent liver carcinogen.
ingredients.notes: IARC Group 1 carcinogen. Strict regulatory limits in all regions. Buy from reputable sources. Store grains and nuts dry.

ingredients.name: ochratoxin a
ingredients.explanation: Mold toxin found in cereals, coffee, and dried fruit. Damages kidneys and is a possible carcinogen.
ingredients.notes: IARC Group 2B. EU has strict limits in cereal and coffee products. Common in improperly dried and stored grains.

ingredients.name: lead
ingredients.explanation: Heavy metal with no safe level. Accumulates in bones. Especially harmful to children's brain development.
ingredients.notes: IARC Group 2A. WHO states no safe level of lead exposure. Strict limits for all food categories globally.

ingredients.name: mercury
ingredients.explanation: Heavy metal found in large fish. Damages nervous system and brain. Especially risky in pregnancy.
ingredients.notes: FDA advises pregnant women to avoid shark, swordfish, tilefish, and king mackerel. High methylmercury content.

ingredients.name: arsenic
ingredients.explanation: Toxic metalloid found in rice and groundwater. Long-term exposure causes cancer and organ damage.
ingredients.notes: IARC Group 1. Inorganic arsenic in rice is a major concern in South Asia. Rinsing rice reduces exposure somewhat.

ingredients.name: cadmium
ingredients.explanation: Heavy metal that accumulates in kidneys. Found in chocolate, leafy greens, and cereals.
ingredients.notes: IARC Group 1. Accumulates in kidneys over decades. EU has set limits in chocolate and cocoa products.

ingredients.name: dioxins
ingredients.explanation: Industrial pollutants that accumulate in fatty foods. Cause cancer and disrupt hormones.
ingredients.notes: IARC Group 1. Found mainly in meat, fish, and dairy fat. Strict EU and US limits in place. Accumulate in body fat.

ingredients.name: caffeine
ingredients.explanation: Naturally occurring stimulant in coffee, tea, and cola. Safe in moderate amounts. Habit-forming.
ingredients.notes: EFSA considers 400mg per day safe for adults. Pregnant women advised to limit to 200mg. Energy drinks must label.

ingredients.name: tea extract
ingredients.explanation: Natural plant extract from tea leaves. Rich in antioxidants and polyphenols. Very safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Concentrated green tea extract supplements at very high doses have caused liver toxicity. Food use is safe.

ingredients.name: coffee extract
ingredients.explanation: Natural extract from roasted coffee beans. Used in flavoring desserts and beverages.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Contains caffeine. Coffee naturally contains acrylamide from roasting. Normal levels are not a concern.

ingredients.name: quinine
ingredients.explanation: Bitter compound from cinchona bark used in tonic water. Strictly limited due to drug-like effects.
ingredients.notes: Limited to 83mg per liter in beverages. Can cause QT prolongation in people with heart conditions. Avoid in pregnancy.

ingredients.name: inulin
ingredients.explanation: Prebiotic fiber from chicory root. Feeds beneficial gut bacteria. Safe at normal food levels.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. High amounts cause gas and bloating. Used in yogurt and protein bars. Excellent gut health ingredient.

ingredients.name: beta glucan
ingredients.explanation: Soluble fiber from oats and barley. Clinically proven to lower LDL cholesterol. Very safe.
ingredients.notes: FDA approved health claim: 3g per day of beta-glucan from oats reduces heart disease risk. EFSA confirmed.

ingredients.name: psyllium husk
ingredients.explanation: Soluble fiber from psyllium seeds. Excellent for digestion and cholesterol. Very safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. FDA-approved cholesterol health claim. Must be taken with plenty of water. Known as isabgol in India.

ingredients.name: omega 3 fatty acids
ingredients.explanation: Essential fatty acids from fish or algae. Proven benefits for heart and brain health.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. FDA allows qualified health claim for heart disease. High doses may thin blood. Algal DHA is vegan-friendly.

ingredients.name: probiotics
ingredients.explanation: Live beneficial bacteria added to yogurt and fermented foods. Support gut health.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. EFSA does not allow health claims on probiotics in EU. Generally safe. Caution in immunocompromised people.

ingredients.name: resveratrol
ingredients.explanation: Natural polyphenol in red grapes and berries. Antioxidant with studied heart health benefits.
ingredients.notes: GRAS at food levels. Supplement doses may interact with blood thinners. Naturally present in wine and grapes.

ingredients.name: astaxanthin
ingredients.explanation: Powerful antioxidant carotenoid from algae. Gives salmon its pink color. Very safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Used in aquaculture and supplements. One of the most potent natural antioxidants known.

ingredients.name: canola oil
ingredients.explanation: Low saturated fat vegetable oil from rapeseed. Heart-healthy fat profile. Widely used.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. FDA-approved heart health claim. Developed to have low erucic acid unlike regular rapeseed oil.

ingredients.name: rice bran oil
ingredients.explanation: Oil from rice bran layer. High smoke point. Contains oryzanol with cholesterol-lowering properties.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Popular in Indian and Asian cooking. FSSAI approved. Contains gamma-oryzanol with studied health benefits.

ingredients.name: corn oil
ingredients.explanation: Vegetable oil from corn germ. High in omega-6 fatty acids. Safe for cooking.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. High omega-6 content may contribute to inflammation if not balanced with omega-3. Usually from GMO corn.

ingredients.name: sodium citrate
ingredients.explanation: Sodium salt of citric acid. Used to buffer acidity in drinks and processed cheese. Safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Very commonly used in sports drinks, soft drinks, and processed cheese. No safety concerns.

ingredients.name: potassium citrate
ingredients.explanation: Potassium salt of citric acid. Used as a buffer and potassium supplement. Very safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Also used medically to treat kidney stones. Lower sodium option vs sodium citrate.

ingredients.name: calcium citrate
ingredients.explanation: Calcium salt of citric acid. Acts as a calcium supplement and acidity regulator. Safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Also a well-absorbed form of calcium supplement. Used in fortified foods and beverages.

ingredients.name: sodium lactate
ingredients.explanation: Sodium salt of lactic acid. Used as a humectant and preservative in meat products.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Used to extend shelf life of cooked meats and poultry. Naturally produced in fermentation.

ingredients.name: potassium lactate
ingredients.explanation: Potassium salt of lactic acid. Lower-sodium alternative to sodium lactate. Safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Used in reduced-sodium meat products. Also a humectant in baked goods.

ingredients.name: calcium lactate
ingredients.explanation: Calcium salt of lactic acid. Used as a firming agent and calcium supplement. Safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Used in fruit preparations and baked goods. Good bioavailability as a calcium supplement.

ingredients.name: calcium acetate
ingredients.explanation: Calcium salt of acetic acid. Acts as a preservative, buffer, and calcium supplement.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Used in baked goods to prevent mold. Also used medically to treat high phosphate in kidney patients.

ingredients.name: sodium acetate
ingredients.explanation: Sodium salt of acetic acid. Gives salt and vinegar chips their tang. Safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Very common in snack food flavoring. Also used as a preservative in baked goods.

ingredients.name: sodium diacetate
ingredients.explanation: Combination of sodium acetate and acetic acid. Mold and bacteria inhibitor in baked goods.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Used in bread and meat products to prevent mold. Releases acetic acid slowly in food.

ingredients.name: sodium malate
ingredients.explanation: Sodium salt of malic acid. Used as a flavor enhancer and acidity regulator. Safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Less common than citric acid but used in confectionery and beverages. No safety concerns.

ingredients.name: calcium malate
ingredients.explanation: Calcium salt of malic acid. Used as a firming agent and calcium supplement. Very safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Used in fruit products and calcium-fortified beverages. Good bioavailability.

ingredients.name: potassium bicarbonate
ingredients.explanation: Potassium-based baking agent and acidity regulator. Sodium-free alternative to baking soda.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Preferred over sodium bicarbonate in low-sodium products. Also used in wine to reduce acidity.

ingredients.name: calcium sulphate
ingredients.explanation: Natural mineral used to firm tofu and regulate acidity in flour. Very safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Key ingredient in making firm tofu. Also used as a calcium supplement in bread and flour.

ingredients.name: ammonium chloride
ingredients.explanation: Used as a yeast nutrient and acidity regulator in bread. Traditional in Nordic salty licorice.
