ingredients.notes: GRAS. Used in yeast-leavened breads. High amounts can cause metabolic issues. Food use levels are safe.

ingredients.name: sodium tartrate
ingredients.explanation: Sodium salt of tartaric acid. Used as an emulsifier and acidity regulator. Safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Less common than potassium tartrate. Used in margarines and baked goods.

ingredients.name: calcium tartrate
ingredients.explanation: Calcium salt of tartaric acid. Used as a food preservative and acidity regulator.
ingredients.notes: EFSA approved. Less widely used. Can precipitate in wine as tartrate crystals. No safety concerns.

ingredients.name: hydrochloric acid
ingredients.explanation: Food-grade dilute acid used in gelatin and starch processing. Safe when neutralized.
ingredients.notes: GRAS as a processing aid. Fully neutralized in the final product. Same acid naturally present in stomach.

ingredients.name: potassium nitrite
ingredients.explanation: Curing agent in processed meats. Forms cancer causing compounds during digestion.
ingredients.notes: IARC Group 2A per nitrite ingestion. Same concerns as sodium nitrite. Used in bacon, ham, cured meats.

ingredients.name: calcium sulfite
ingredients.explanation: Sulfite preservative used in wine and fruit products. Same asthma risks as other sulfites.
ingredients.notes: Part of the sulfites group. Mandatory labeling when above threshold. Asthma trigger in sensitive individuals.

ingredients.name: calcium bisulfite
ingredients.explanation: Sulfite preservative used in wine making and fruit preservation. Asthma concern.
ingredients.notes: Sulfite group member. Mandatory labeling required. Less common than sodium or potassium sulfites.

ingredients.name: potassium sulfite
ingredients.explanation: Sulfite preservative used in wine and food products. Same asthma and allergy concerns as other sulfites.
ingredients.notes: Sulfite group. All sulfites must be declared when present above 10ppm in EU and US.

ingredients.name: cyclamate
ingredients.explanation: Artificial sweetener banned in the US since 1969. Still used in EU and India. Cancer concerns.
ingredients.notes: FDA banned in 1969 after animal cancer studies. EFSA reviewed and allows with ADI. CSPI rates Avoid.

ingredients.name: advantame
ingredients.explanation: Newer high-intensity sweetener, 20000 times sweeter than sugar. Very safe based on current data.
ingredients.notes: FDA approved in 2014. EFSA approved in 2013. Derived from aspartame but does not require PKU warning.

ingredients.name: aspartame acesulfame salt
ingredients.explanation: Combination sweetener of aspartame and acesulfame. Concerns from aspartame component.
ingredients.notes: Contains aspartame. Must carry PKU warning. EFSA reviewed 2023 and maintains current ADI for aspartame.

ingredients.name: alitame
ingredients.explanation: High-intensity sweetener 2000 times sweeter than sugar. Approved in limited markets only.
ingredients.notes: Approved in Australia, New Zealand, China, Mexico. Not yet approved in US or EU. Safety data looks positive.

ingredients.name: mannitol
ingredients.explanation: Sugar alcohol naturally found in mushrooms and seaweed. Used in sugar-free products. Safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Laxative effect at high doses. Used in chewing gum and diabetic foods. Also used medically.

ingredients.name: hydrogenated starch hydrolysate
ingredients.explanation: Mixture of sugar alcohols from starch. Used in sugar-free candy and gum. Lower calorie.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Laxative effect in large amounts. Commonly used in sugar-free and diabetic confectionery.

ingredients.name: gluconic acid
ingredients.explanation: Mild natural acid from glucose oxidation. Used in cleaning and food applications. Very safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Naturally found in honey, wine, and fruit. Very mild acid. Also used as a mineral carrier.

ingredients.name: sodium gluconate
ingredients.explanation: Sodium salt of gluconic acid. Used as a sequestrant and mineral supplement carrier.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Used to carry minerals like iron and zinc in fortified foods. No safety concerns.

ingredients.name: potassium gluconate
ingredients.explanation: Potassium salt of gluconic acid. Used as a potassium supplement and acidity regulator.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Also a well-absorbed potassium supplement. Used in sports drinks and electrolyte products.

ingredients.name: calcium gluconate
ingredients.explanation: Calcium salt of gluconic acid. Used as a firming agent and calcium supplement. Safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Also used as an intravenous calcium supplement medically. Food use levels are completely safe.

ingredients.name: magnesium chloride
ingredients.explanation: Mineral salt used to make tofu and as a magnesium supplement. Very safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Known as nigari in Japanese tofu-making. Key coagulant in traditional tofu production.

ingredients.name: broccoli
ingredients.explanation: Cruciferous vegetable rich in vitamin C, K, and sulforaphane. Excellent nutrition. Very safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Sulforaphane has studied cancer-protective properties. May affect thyroid in very large raw amounts.

ingredients.name: cauliflower
ingredients.explanation: Cruciferous vegetable high in fiber and vitamins. Versatile and safe for most people.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Goitrogenic compounds but only a concern at extremely high raw intake. Universally safe in cooked form.

ingredients.name: cabbage
ingredients.explanation: Cruciferous vegetable rich in vitamin C and fiber. Safe and widely consumed globally.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Used raw in slaws and cooked in curries. Fermented as sauerkraut for probiotic benefits.

ingredients.name: peas
ingredients.explanation: Protein and fiber-rich vegetable legume. Used fresh and dried. Very safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. One of the most nutritious vegetables. Frozen peas retain nutrients very well.

ingredients.name: sweet corn
ingredients.explanation: Sweet variety of corn. Good source of fiber and B vitamins. Safe for most people.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Most commercial sweet corn in the US is GMO. Organic and non-GMO options available.

ingredients.name: beetroot
ingredients.explanation: Root vegetable rich in nitrates, folate, and antioxidants. May lower blood pressure.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. High oxalate content. Kidney stone patients should moderate. Urine pinking (beeturia) is harmless.

ingredients.name: eggplant
ingredients.explanation: Nightshade vegetable rich in antioxidants and fiber. Safe when cooked. Do not eat raw.
ingredients.notes: GRAS when cooked. Raw eggplant contains solanine. Cooking eliminates this concern completely.

ingredients.name: okra
ingredients.explanation: Fiber and folate-rich vegetable. The mucilage helps lower blood sugar. Very safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. High in soluble fiber. Popular across India. Contains oxalates but at safe food levels.

ingredients.name: bitter gourd
ingredients.explanation: Bitter vegetable with blood sugar lowering properties. Seeds and rind can be toxic in excess.
ingredients.notes: FSSAI approved. Seeds contain vicine which can cause issues in G6PD-deficient individuals. Fruit flesh is safe.

ingredients.name: drumstick vegetable
ingredients.explanation: Long green pods from moringa tree. Rich in vitamins and minerals. Very safe.
ingredients.notes: FSSAI approved. Different from moringa leaves already in DB. High in calcium and iron.

ingredients.name: strawberry
ingredients.explanation: Berry rich in vitamin C and antioxidants. Safe for most people. Rare allergen.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Strawberry allergy exists but is uncommon. High pesticide residue possible on non-organic.

ingredients.name: blueberry
ingredients.explanation: Antioxidant-rich berry. One of the most studied health foods. Very safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. High in anthocyanins. Studied for cognitive health benefits. Blood thinner interactions possible at very high doses.

ingredients.name: pineapple
ingredients.explanation: Tropical fruit rich in vitamin C and bromelain enzyme. Safe and widely consumed.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Bromelain in raw pineapple can irritate mouth lining in large amounts. Cooked or canned pineapple is milder.

ingredients.name: papaya
ingredients.explanation: Tropical fruit rich in vitamin C, A, and papain enzyme. Safe and digestive-friendly.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Unripe papaya should be avoided in pregnancy. Ripe papaya is safe and nutritious for all.

ingredients.name: guava
ingredients.explanation: Tropical fruit with very high vitamin C content. Rich in fiber. Very safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. One of the richest sources of vitamin C. Seeds are edible and rich in fiber.

ingredients.name: pomegranate
ingredients.explanation: Fruit rich in punicalagins and antioxidants. Safe but may interact with medications.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Pomegranate juice may interact with blood thinners and statins. Fruit itself is very safe.

ingredients.name: jackfruit
ingredients.explanation: Large tropical fruit used as a meat substitute. Rich in fiber and vitamins. Very safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Young jackfruit mimics pulled meat texture. Ripe fruit is sweet and nutritious. Common in India.

ingredients.name: litchi
ingredients.explanation: Sweet tropical fruit. Unripe litchi on empty stomach linked to hypoglycemic illness in children.
ingredients.notes: Ripe litchi is safe for adults. WHO linked unripe litchi to toxic hypoglycemia in malnourished children in India.

ingredients.name: watermelon
ingredients.explanation: Hydrating fruit rich in lycopene and vitamins. Safe for all ages.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Very high water content. Natural source of citrulline. No known safety concerns.

ingredients.name: coconut water
ingredients.explanation: Natural electrolyte drink from young coconuts. Excellent hydration. Very safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Natural source of potassium. Those with kidney disease should monitor potassium intake.

ingredients.name: mint
ingredients.explanation: Aromatic herb with menthol as active compound. Used in chutneys and beverages. Very safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Peppermint oil in large amounts can cause heartburn. Fresh mint in cooking is completely safe.

ingredients.name: coriander leaves
ingredients.explanation: Fresh herb used widely in Indian cooking. Rich in antioxidants. Very safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Some people perceive cilantro as soapy due to genetic variation. No safety concerns at all.

ingredients.name: basil
ingredients.explanation: Aromatic herb rich in antioxidants and essential oils. Safe in food amounts.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. High estragole content in basil essential oil at very high doses. Normal food use is safe.

ingredients.name: thyme
ingredients.explanation: Aromatic herb with thymol as active compound. Antimicrobial properties. Safe in food amounts.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Thyme oil is concentrated and should not be taken internally. Culinary amounts are safe.

ingredients.name: rosemary
ingredients.explanation: Aromatic Mediterranean herb with antioxidant properties. Safe in food amounts.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Rosemary extract is also used as a natural antioxidant (E392). Culinary use is completely safe.

ingredients.name: oregano
ingredients.explanation: Pungent herb used in Mediterranean cooking. Rich in antioxidants. Very safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Oregano oil has high carvacrol and thymol content. Concentrated oil can interact with blood thinners.

ingredients.name: carom seeds
ingredients.explanation: Indian spice with thymol as active compound. Aids digestion. Very safe in food amounts.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Used in Indian bread and snacks. Thymol content makes it naturally antimicrobial. Safe at culinary levels.

ingredients.name: fennel seeds
ingredients.explanation: Licorice-flavored seeds used in Indian cooking and as a mouth freshener. Safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Estragole content at food levels is not a concern. Used in chai, curries, and as a digestive.

ingredients.name: long pepper
ingredients.explanation: Ancient Indian spice related to black pepper. Used in Ayurvedic medicine. Safe.
ingredients.notes: FSSAI approved. Used in trikatu (three-pepper blend) in Ayurveda. Stronger flavor than black pepper.

ingredients.name: white pepper
ingredients.explanation: Ripe black pepper with outer skin removed. Milder flavor than black pepper. Safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Same plant as black pepper. Used in white sauces where black specks are undesirable.

ingredients.name: red chili powder
ingredients.explanation: Dried ground chili pepper. Rich in capsaicin and vitamin C. Safe in normal amounts.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Adulteration with Sudan red dye is a concern in India. Buy from reputable brands. Kashmiri variety is mild.

ingredients.name: asafoetida compound
ingredients.explanation: Commercial hing diluted with wheat flour and starch for ease of use. Safe for most people.
ingredients.notes: FSSAI regulated. Contains wheat flour. Celiac and wheat-allergic people must use pure resin hing instead.

ingredients.name: mustard seeds
ingredients.explanation: Pungent seeds widely used in Indian tempering. Rich in selenium and omega-3. Safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Mustard allergy is a major allergen in EU. Must be declared on labels in Europe.

ingredients.name: garam masala blend
ingredients.explanation: Ready-mix blend of warm spices. Variable composition by brand. Generally safe.
ingredients.notes: FSSAI regulated as blended spice. Quality and adulteration concerns for unbranded products.

ingredients.name: peppercorn mix
aliases: black white pink green pepper blend
ingredients.explanation: Blend of black, white, pink and green peppercorns. Safe combination spice product.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Pink pepper is from a different plant (schinus) and is technically not true pepper. All are safe.

ingredients.name: kokum extract
ingredients.explanation: Concentrated extract from kokum rind. Used in syrups and confectionery. Very safe.
ingredients.notes: FSSAI approved. Hydroxycitric acid content has been studied for weight management. Food use is safe.

ingredients.name: tamarind concentrate
ingredients.explanation: Concentrated tamarind paste. Same safety as tamarind. Convenient form for cooking.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Intensified form of tamarind. High in tartaric acid. No safety concerns at culinary levels.

ingredients.name: vinegar malt
ingredients.explanation: Fermented grain-based vinegar. Contains acetic acid. Used as condiment and preservative.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Malt vinegar contains gluten traces. People with celiac should use distilled white vinegar instead.

ingredients.name: avocado oil
ingredients.explanation: Premium oil from avocado flesh. Very high smoke point. Rich in monounsaturated fats.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. One of the healthiest cooking oils. High oleic acid content. Good for high-heat cooking.

ingredients.name: flaxseed oil
ingredients.explanation: Rich source of plant-based omega-3 (ALA). Cold-pressed and sensitive to heat. Very safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Not suitable for cooking due to low smoke point. Best used cold in dressings. Oxidizes quickly.

ingredients.name: walnut oil
ingredients.explanation: Delicate oil from walnuts. Rich in omega-3 and antioxidants. Best used cold. Safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Tree nut allergen. Best for salad dressings. Goes rancid quickly. Store refrigerated.

ingredients.name: almond oil
ingredients.explanation: Mild oil from sweet almonds. Rich in vitamin E. Used in cooking and cosmetics.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Tree nut allergen. Refined almond oil has neutral flavor. Used in Indian sweets and confectionery.

ingredients.name: hemp seed oil
ingredients.explanation: Nutritious oil from hemp seeds. Perfect 3:1 omega-6 to omega-3 ratio. Contains no THC.
ingredients.notes: GRAS in US and EU. India has restrictions on hemp products. Zero THC content in cold-pressed seed oil.

ingredients.name: cottonseed oil
ingredients.explanation: Oil from cotton seeds. Contains gossypol in unrefined form. Widely used but has concerns.
ingredients.notes: CSPI rates Caution. Refined cottonseed oil is safe. Unrefined contains gossypol which can cause infertility issues.

ingredients.name: pumpkin seed oil
ingredients.explanation: Dark green oil from roasted pumpkin seeds. Rich in zinc and antioxidants. Very safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Popular in Central European cuisine. Studied for prostate and bladder health. Best used cold.

ingredients.name: nigella oil
ingredients.explanation: Oil from black cumin seeds. Rich in thymoquinone with studied therapeutic properties. Safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Revered in Islamic medicine. High doses may interact with blood thinners. Food amounts are safe.

ingredients.name: cream
ingredients.explanation: High-fat dairy product skimmed from milk. Used in cooking and desserts. Safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. High in saturated fat. FSSAI regulates fat percentage standards. Not suitable for lactose intolerant or dairy allergic.

ingredients.name: cheese
ingredients.explanation: Fermented dairy product in many varieties. Rich in protein and calcium. Generally safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. High in sodium and saturated fat. Aged cheeses contain tyramine which can trigger migraines. Lactose intolerant people vary.

ingredients.name: sour cream
ingredients.explanation: Cream fermented with lactic acid bacteria. Tangy flavor. Safe for most people.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. High in saturated fat. Contains live cultures. Not suitable for lactose intolerant or dairy allergic.

ingredients.name: soy milk
ingredients.explanation: Plant milk from soybeans. Closest nutritional profile to cow milk. Safe for most people.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Major soy allergen. Most complete plant protein. Contains phytoestrogens. Safe at normal consumption.

ingredients.name: almond milk
ingredients.explanation: Diluted almond beverage. Low calorie and lactose-free. Tree nut allergen concern.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Tree nut allergen. Very low protein compared to cow milk. Usually fortified with calcium and vitamins.

ingredients.name: oat milk
ingredients.explanation: Creamy plant milk from oats. Naturally sweet. Good for barista use. Safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Not suitable for celiac unless labeled gluten-free. Lower protein than soy milk. Popular worldwide.

ingredients.name: rice milk
ingredients.explanation: Most hypoallergenic plant milk. Very low protein. Safe for almost everyone.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. FDA advises toddlers not to use rice milk as main drink due to low nutrition. Contains trace arsenic.

ingredients.name: egg white
ingredients.explanation: Protein-rich egg white. Used in meringues and as a fat-free protein source. Safe when cooked.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Major egg allergen. Raw egg white contains avidin which blocks biotin. Cooking neutralizes avidin.

ingredients.name: whole egg powder
ingredients.explanation: Dehydrated whole eggs used in baking and food manufacturing. Same nutrition as fresh eggs.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Major egg allergen. Pasteurized so safer than raw eggs. Used in commercial baked goods.

ingredients.name: wheat bran
ingredients.explanation: Outer layer of wheat grain. Very high in fiber. Good for digestive health.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Contains gluten. Not suitable for celiac. High phytic acid can reduce mineral absorption if not soaked.

ingredients.name: maida
ingredients.explanation: Refined white flour stripped of fiber and nutrients. High glycemic. Linked to metabolic issues.
ingredients.notes: GRAS but nutritionally inferior. High glycemic index. FSSAI mandates fortification with vitamins. Contains gluten.

ingredients.name: buckwheat
ingredients.explanation: Gluten-free pseudo-cereal. High in protein, fiber, and minerals. Safe for celiac patients.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Despite the name, it is gluten-free and not related to wheat. Used in Hindu fasting foods in India.

ingredients.name: rajma
ingredients.explanation: Protein and fiber-rich kidney beans. Must be cooked thoroughly. Safe when properly cooked.
ingredients.notes: GRAS when cooked. Raw kidney beans contain phytohaemagglutinin toxin. Boiling for 10 minutes destroys it completely.

ingredients.name: black beans
ingredients.explanation: Fiber and protein-rich legume. Popular in Mexican cuisine. Safe when cooked.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Same cooking precautions as kidney beans. Excellent plant protein source.

ingredients.name: lentils
ingredients.explanation: Small protein-rich legumes. Fast-cooking and highly nutritious. Very safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. One of the most nutritious foods in the world. High iron content. Common in Indian and Middle Eastern cooking.

ingredients.name: chickpeas
ingredients.explanation: Versatile legume rich in protein and fiber. Used whole or as besan. Very safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Chickpea allergy exists but is uncommon. Sprouting reduces antinutrients and increases bioavailability.

ingredients.name: golden syrup
ingredients.explanation: Light amber syrup from sugar refining. Mild buttery flavor. Used in baking. Safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Lower in minerals than treacle. Similar to corn syrup but with a more complex flavor.

ingredients.name: stevia leaf
ingredients.explanation: Dried stevia leaves used as natural sweetener. Safe at food levels.
ingredients.notes: GRAS for purified steviol glycosides. Whole leaf stevia is not FDA approved as food additive. Purified form is.

ingredients.name: rosemary extract
ingredients.explanation: Natural antioxidant from rosemary. Used to prevent fat oxidation in foods. Very safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Natural alternative to synthetic antioxidants BHA and BHT. EFSA approved. No known concerns.

ingredients.name: ethoxyquin
ingredients.explanation: Synthetic antioxidant used in fish meal and spices. Banned in EU for food use. Safety concerns.
ingredients.notes: CSPI rates Avoid. EU banned as food additive. FDA limits use in animal feed. Concerns about liver toxicity.

ingredients.name: calcium ascorbate
ingredients.explanation: Calcium salt of vitamin C. Non-acidic form of vitamin C used as antioxidant and supplement.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Gentler on stomach than regular vitamin C. Provides both calcium and vitamin C benefits.

ingredients.name: iron oxide black
ingredients.explanation: Mineral pigment used to color olives and confectionery. Safe at regulated levels.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Used in decorative food coloring. Not absorbed by the body. Strict limits apply.

ingredients.name: iron oxide red
ingredients.explanation: Mineral-derived red pigment used in salmon-colored products. Safe at regulated levels.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Natural iron-based color. Used in dried fruits and some sausage casings. Not absorbed.

ingredients.name: iron oxide yellow
ingredients.explanation: Yellow mineral pigment used as a food coloring. Safe at regulated levels.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Natural iron-based color. Used in pasta and bakery products for golden color.

ingredients.name: gold
ingredients.explanation: Pure gold used decoratively on food. Chemically inert and passes through the body unchanged.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Biologically inert. Very expensive. Used in luxury confectionery and Indian sweets (vark concept).

ingredients.name: silver
ingredients.explanation: Pure silver used decoratively on Indian sweets. Traditionally used as vark. Generally safe.
ingredients.notes: FSSAI regulates purity of vark. Concerns exist about adulteration with aluminum in commercial vark products.

ingredients.name: riboflavin sodium phosphate
ingredients.explanation: Water-soluble form of riboflavin used as a yellow food color and B2 vitamin supplement.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. More water-soluble than plain riboflavin. Used in beverages and dairy products.

ingredients.name: yeast extract flavor
ingredients.explanation: Concentrated yeast extract with rich umami flavor. Natural and widely used. Safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. High in naturally occurring glutamates but not classified as MSG. Rich in B vitamins.

ingredients.name: maltol
ingredients.explanation: Natural flavor compound that enhances sweetness and caramel notes. Safe at food levels.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Naturally found in roasted malt, coffee, and bread crust. Used to enhance sweetness in low-sugar products.

ingredients.name: ethyl maltol
ingredients.explanation: Synthetic version of maltol. Five times more potent sweetness enhancer. Safe at food levels.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Used in confectionery, beverages, and tobacco. JECFA ADI established. No known concerns.

ingredients.name: lanolin
ingredients.explanation: Natural wax from sheep wool used as a coating on fruit. Generally safe.
ingredients.notes: Not vegan. Derived from sheep wool. Used on some citrus fruits and confectionery. Allergy rare but possible.

ingredients.name: microcrystalline wax
ingredients.explanation: Refined petroleum wax used as a coating on fruits and confectionery. Not digestible.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Passes through body undigested. Used on citrus fruits to reduce moisture loss. Strict purity standards.

ingredients.name: polyvinylpyrrolidone
ingredients.explanation: Synthetic polymer used as a clarifying agent in wine and beer. Not absorbed by the body.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Used in wine fining and tablet coatings. Not absorbed. Removed from wine before bottling.

ingredients.name: polydextrose
ingredients.explanation: Synthetic soluble fiber from glucose. Used as a low-calorie bulking agent. Safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Laxative effect at doses above 50g per day. Acts as a prebiotic at lower doses. Common in diet foods.

ingredients.name: oxidised polyethylene
ingredients.explanation: Synthetic wax used to coat fresh citrus fruits to prevent moisture loss. Not digested.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Not absorbed. Used on citrus fruits and some vegetables. Wash fruit before peeling.

ingredients.name: sulfuric acid
ingredients.explanation: Food-grade acid used in starch and glucose syrup processing. Fully neutralized in final product.
ingredients.notes: GRAS as processing aid only. Not present in final food product. Used in glucose syrup production.

ingredients.name: sodium hydroxide
ingredients.explanation: Strong alkali used to cure olives, make pretzels, and process cocoa. Neutralized in food.
ingredients.notes: GRAS as processing aid. Makes pretzels brown and chewy. Cures ramen noodles. Fully neutralized in final product.

ingredients.name: propane
ingredients.explanation: Food-grade propellant gas used in aerosol food sprays. Safe at food use levels.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Used in cooking sprays and whipped cream cans. Flammable. Not consumed directly.

ingredients.name: nitrous oxide
ingredients.explanation: Gas propellant used in whipped cream chargers. Safe in food use. Very low exposure.
ingredients.notes: GRAS as food propellant. The tiny amount in whipped cream is safe. Misuse as recreational drug is not a food safety issue.

ingredients.name: oxygen
ingredients.explanation: Used in modified atmosphere packaging for fresh meat to maintain red color. Safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Natural component of air. Used to maintain meat color in MAP packaging. No safety concerns.

ingredients.name: carob bean gum
ingredients.explanation: Gum from carob seeds. Same family as locust bean gum. Natural thickener. Very safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Functionally very similar to locust bean gum. Used in ice cream and cheese. Infant formula approved.

ingredients.name: tapioca starch
ingredients.explanation: Starch from cassava root. Gluten-free and neutral flavor. Excellent thickener. Very safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Pure starch with minimal nutrition. Gluten-free. Used in bubble tea, puddings, and gluten-free baking.

ingredients.name: arrowroot starch
ingredients.explanation: Pure starch from arrowroot plant. Gluten-free and easy to digest. Very safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Easy to digest. Good for infants and elderly. Used in biscuits and as a thickener in Indian cooking.

ingredients.name: waxy maize starch
ingredients.explanation: High-amylopectin corn starch with excellent freeze-thaw stability. Safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Better freeze-thaw stability than regular corn starch. Used in frozen foods and retort products.

ingredients.name: diacetin
ingredients.explanation: Glycerol derivative used as a humectant and solvent in food. Safe at food levels.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Used in flavoring preparations and as a plasticizer in food packaging materials.

ingredients.name: triacetin
ingredients.explanation: Glycerol ester used as a humectant and solvent for flavors. Safe at normal food use.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Used in flavoring preparations and chewing gum. Also used in pharmaceutical tablet coatings.

ingredients.name: ethyl cellulose
ingredients.explanation: Modified cellulose used as a film-forming and coating agent. Not digested. Safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Used in slow-release coatings on tablets and in confectionery coatings. Passes through body unchanged.

ingredients.name: cross-linked sodium carboxymethyl cellulose
ingredients.explanation: Cross-linked form of CMC used as a disintegrant and thickener. Very safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Used in tablet formulations and food thickening. Passes through body without absorption.

ingredients.name: acacia fiber
ingredients.explanation: Soluble dietary fiber from acacia gum. Excellent prebiotic and thickener. Very safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. FDA approved for fiber claim. Excellent prebiotic. Much higher fiber content than most plant sources.

ingredients.name: chicory root extract
ingredients.explanation: Inulin-rich extract from chicory root. Natural prebiotic and coffee substitute. Safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Used as coffee substitute and prebiotic fiber. Gas and bloating possible at high doses. Generally safe.

ingredients.name: locust bean gum variant
ingredients.explanation: Alternative seed gum used as a thickener in dairy and meat. Safe and well-reviewed.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Similar to locust bean gum but from tara plant. Good protein binding in meat applications.

ingredients.name: green tea
ingredients.explanation: Unoxidized tea leaves rich in catechins and EGCG. One of the most studied health drinks.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Contains caffeine and tannins. Catechins are powerful antioxidants. Very high doses of supplements can cause liver issues.

ingredients.name: black tea
ingredients.explanation: Fully oxidized tea. Rich in theaflavins and thearubigins. Safe and widely consumed.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Contains caffeine. Tannins can reduce iron absorption if drunk with meals. Very safe at normal intake.

ingredients.name: chamomile extract
ingredients.explanation: Floral herb extract used in teas and beverages. Anti-inflammatory properties. Safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Rare allergy in people sensitive to Asteraceae family plants. Widely used in herbal teas.

ingredients.name: hibiscus extract
ingredients.explanation: Deep red extract from hibiscus flowers. Rich in anthocyanins. May lower blood pressure.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. May interact with blood pressure medications. Studies show antihypertensive effects. Natural red color source.

ingredients.name: stevia extract
ingredients.explanation: Purified sweet compounds from stevia leaves. Zero calorie natural sweetener. Safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS for purified steviol glycosides. Reb A most widely used. May have slight bitter aftertaste.

ingredients.name: glucosamine
ingredients.explanation: Amino sugar naturally found in cartilage. Used in joint health supplements. Generally safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Often shellfish-derived. Shellfish-allergic individuals should use synthetic or fermentation-derived versions.

ingredients.name: coenzyme q10
ingredients.explanation: Natural antioxidant produced by the body. Used in functional foods and supplements. Safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. May interact with blood thinners. Generally safe and well-tolerated. Found naturally in meat and fish.

ingredients.name: lutein
ingredients.explanation: Yellow carotenoid from marigold flowers. Supports eye health. Natural color. Very safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Studied for macular degeneration prevention. Used as natural yellow color in foods and supplements.

ingredients.name: zeaxanthin
ingredients.explanation: Yellow-orange carotenoid that supports eye health. Natural color. Safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Works with lutein for macular protection. Found in corn, egg yolk, and dark leafy greens.

ingredients.name: quercetin
ingredients.explanation: Plant flavonoid with antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties. Natural and safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Found in onions, apples, and berries. High supplement doses may interact with certain medications.

ingredients.name: lycopene tomato
ingredients.explanation: Red carotenoid from tomato. Studied for prostate health benefits. Natural color. Safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Both natural tomato extract and synthetic forms are approved. Bioavailability improved by cooking with fat.

ingredients.name: ashwagandha
ingredients.explanation: Ayurvedic adaptogen. May reduce stress and anxiety. Not fully approved for food use globally.
ingredients.notes: FSSAI allows in nutraceuticals. EU has safety concerns. May interact with thyroid medication and sedatives.

ingredients.name: turmeric milk
ingredients.explanation: Traditional Indian drink combining milk and turmeric. Both ingredients are safe.
ingredients.notes: FSSAI approved as a traditional food. Trending globally as golden milk. Combined benefits of turmeric and dairy.

ingredients.name: triphala
ingredients.explanation: Traditional Ayurvedic blend of three fruits. Mild laxative and antioxidant properties.
ingredients.notes: FSSAI approved nutraceutical. Mild laxative effect. Long traditional use record in India. Avoid in pregnancy.

ingredients.name: creatine
ingredients.explanation: Naturally found in meat and fish. Well-studied sports supplement. Safe at normal doses.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. One of the most researched supplements. Dose above 5g per day may stress kidneys in some individuals.

ingredients.name: l-carnitine
ingredients.explanation: Amino acid derivative that helps transport fatty acids. Used in sports foods. Safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Naturally found in meat. Some studies suggest high intake may increase TMAO, affecting heart health. Dietary amounts are safe.

ingredients.name: taurine
ingredients.explanation: Amino acid naturally in meat and seafood. Used in energy drinks. Safe at normal levels.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Added to energy drinks and infant formula. Very well studied. No safety issues at food use levels.

ingredients.name: branched chain amino acids
ingredients.explanation: Essential amino acids leucine, isoleucine, and valine. Used in sports nutrition. Safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Found naturally in all protein foods. Supplements have good safety profile. Excessive doses not well-studied.

ingredients.name: guarana extract
ingredients.explanation: South American plant extract very high in caffeine. More potent than coffee. Caution needed.
ingredients.notes: EFSA recommends cumulative caffeine monitoring. Commonly in energy drinks. Pregnant women should avoid.

ingredients.name: yerba mate
ingredients.explanation: South American caffeinated herbal drink. High caffeine and polyphenol content. Linked to esophageal cancer when drunk very hot.
ingredients.notes: IARC 2A classification is for very hot beverages as a category, not yerba mate itself. Moderate maintained for caffeine and temperature concerns. IARC Group 2A for very hot beverages. Yerba mate itself not classified separately. Heavy long-term users at higher risk.

ingredients.name: acai extract
ingredients.explanation: Antioxidant-rich Amazonian berry extract. Safe as food ingredient.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Extremely high antioxidant ORAC value. No safety concerns. Popular in smoothies and superfood products.

ingredients.name: goji berry
ingredients.explanation: Antioxidant-rich berry from China. Safe as food. May interact with warfarin.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. May increase effect of blood-thinning medications. Otherwise safe and nutritious. Popular in health foods.

ingredients.name: noni extract
ingredients.explanation: Tropical fruit extract used as a health supplement. Liver toxicity reported at very high doses.
ingredients.notes: EU novel food approval. Rare liver toxicity cases reported. Normal food consumption is safe. Avoid high-dose supplements.

ingredients.name: amaranth grain
ingredients.explanation: Gluten-free ancient grain with complete protein. Used in Indian fasting foods. Very safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Not related to red 2 dye also called amaranth. Nutrient-dense pseudo-cereal. Gluten-free. Used during Navratri.

ingredients.name: hemp seeds
ingredients.explanation: Nutrient-dense seeds with complete protein and ideal omega ratio. Very safe. No THC.
ingredients.notes: GRAS in US and EU. India has restrictions on hemp products. Seeds are nutritious with negligible THC.

ingredients.name: poppy seeds
ingredients.explanation: Tiny seeds used in Indian and European cooking. Rich in calcium and minerals. Safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Contain trace opiates but amounts in food are negligible. Some countries have import restrictions.

ingredients.name: lotus seeds
ingredients.explanation: Puffed lotus seeds used as a low-calorie snack in India. Rich in protein and minerals.
ingredients.notes: FSSAI approved. Excellent low-calorie, high-protein snack. Popular in Ayurvedic cooking. No safety concerns.

ingredients.name: melon seeds
ingredients.explanation: Seeds from muskmelon used in Indian cooking and sweets. Rich in protein and fat. Safe.
ingredients.notes: FSSAI approved. Used in traditional Indian sweets and as a cooling ingredient in summer drinks.

ingredients.name: macadamia nuts
ingredients.explanation: Creamy tree nut very high in monounsaturated fats. Safe for people. Toxic to dogs.
ingredients.notes: GRAS for humans. Tree nut allergen. Extremely toxic to dogs. Highest fat content of any nut.

ingredients.name: brazil nuts
ingredients.explanation: Rich in selenium. One or two per day meets selenium needs. More can cause selenium toxicity.
ingredients.notes: Tree nut allergen. Limit to 1-3 per day. Very high selenium can cause selenosis at excessive intake.

ingredients.name: pine nuts
ingredients.explanation: Seeds from pine trees. Rich in healthy fats and iron. Safe. Rare pine mouth syndrome.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Tree nut allergen. Pine mouth syndrome causes bitter taste for days after eating certain varieties. Harmless but unusual.

ingredients.name: pecan
ingredients.explanation: Tree nut native to North America. Rich in antioxidants and healthy fats. Safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Tree nut allergen. Rich in oleic acid. Heart-healthy nut with good antioxidant profile.

ingredients.name: chestnut
ingredients.explanation: Starchy tree nut with low fat. Often cooked. Gluten-free and nutritious. Very safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Unlike other nuts, chestnuts are low in fat and high in starch. Gluten-free flour option.

ingredients.name: edamame
ingredients.explanation: Young soybeans harvested before maturity. Rich in protein and fiber. Safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Major soy allergen. High in complete protein. Popular in Japanese cuisine and increasingly in India.

ingredients.name: tofu
ingredients.explanation: Coagulated soy milk formed into blocks. Excellent plant protein. Safe for most people.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Major soy allergen. Contains phytoestrogens. Normal consumption is safe for all age groups.

ingredients.name: tempeh
ingredients.explanation: Fermented soybean product from Indonesia. Higher protein and more digestible than tofu.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Major soy allergen. Fermentation reduces phytic acid. Rich in vitamin B12 precursors.

ingredients.name: miso
ingredients.explanation: Traditional Japanese fermented soy paste. Rich in umami and probiotics. Safe.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Major soy allergen. Very high sodium. Contains live cultures. Used in soups and marinades globally.

ingredients.name: cellulose
ingredients.explanation: Plant fiber used as a thickener. Safe. Found naturally in all plants.
ingredients.notes: GRAS. Different from carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC) which is chemically modified.

ingredients.name: wheat flour
ingredients.explanation: A basic cooking ingredient. Safe. Contains gluten.
ingredients.notes: Allergen for celiac disease. Different from maida (refined/bleached flour).

ingredients.name: mustard
ingredients.explanation: A natural spice. Safe. Allergen for some people.
ingredients.notes: Different from mustard oil which contains erucic acid.

ingredients.name: potato
ingredients.explanation: A common starchy vegetable used whole or dried in many snack foods.

ingredients.name: edible vegetable oil
ingredients.explanation: Generic term for refined plant-based cooking oil (often sunflower, palm, or a blend). Safe staple.
ingredients.notes: Label may not specify the exact source oil.

ingredients.name: spices
ingredients.explanation: Generic term for a blend of culinary spices. Safe staple.
